what_this_is: The formula in words for every function an outside model is asked to judge and test: how the function gets its answer, every number included. Written by reading the function. read_from is the fingerprint of the function it was read from; build-outside-test-cards.py stops when a function changes until its rule is read again (--reread <id>).

MK-CF-F-001.name: buildBudgetState
MK-CF-F-001.rule: Projected to save = monthly take-home − monthly planned expenses (0 when none is stored).

MK-CF-F-002.name: plannedMonthlySpend
MK-CF-F-002.rule: The larger of two figures: the budget categories added up (spendBuckets), and the single monthly figure the person typed.

MK-CF-F-003.name: categoryMonthly
MK-CF-F-003.rule: 0 when the amount is zero or less. A dollar category: the amount, per month — a once-a-year (non-monthly) category is the yearly amount ÷ 12. A percent category: that percent of the average monthly take-home (pctBaseMonthly) — for a non-monthly one the same, worked as a yearly amount and ÷ 12.

MK-CF-F-004.name: spendBuckets
MK-CF-F-004.rule: With categories: each category's monthly amount (categoryMonthly) is added into fixed, non-monthly or flexible — any other bucket counts as flexible; rows of zero are skipped. With no categories: the three typed bucket totals. Monthly total = the three added.

MK-CF-F-005.name: actualMonthFlow
MK-CF-F-005.rule: Rows, in this order. Actual inflow = the monthly take-home handed in. One row for each debt with a required payment above zero: minus what was logged as paid against it this month (0 when nothing was), marked paid or not. Other debt payments = debt payments logged this month that match no debt on record, when above zero. Expenses entered by hand = minus the month's logged expenses that were not imported, debt payments left out. Expenses imported from your card = minus the imported ones, shown only when there are any. Debts on the big-ticket radar (cards, lines of credit, debts due in full) are moved to the end. Surplus = every row added up.

MK-CF-F-006.name: allocatableThisMonth
MK-CF-F-006.rule: Surplus − what has already been set aside this month; never below 0.

MK-CF-F-007.name: nonMonthlyBasis
MK-CF-F-007.rule: True, with the percents added and rounded to a whole number, only when there is at least one non-monthly category above zero and every one of them is entered as a percent. Otherwise false and 0.

MK-CF-F-008.name: spendByMonth
MK-CF-F-008.rule: Twelve calendar months. Each monthly category adds its monthly amount to every month (a percent category = that percent of the average monthly take-home). Each non-monthly category adds its yearly amount spread evenly over the months it names — over all twelve when it names none (a percent one = percent × average monthly take-home × 12). With no categories: the three typed buckets' total, every month. Then, when the single typed monthly figure is larger than the categories' monthly total, the difference is added to every month.

MK-CF-F-009.name: monthlyEssentials
MK-CF-F-009.rule: With no categories: the planned monthly expenses (plannedMonthlySpend). With categories: the monthly categories marked as needs — every one except those marked flexible, a category with no mark counting as flexible, and non-monthly ones left out — added up (a percent one = percent of the average monthly take-home), plus the amount by which the typed monthly figure exceeds the categories' total.

MK-CF-F-010.name: emergencyTest
MK-CF-F-010.rule: Essentials = the figure handed in when above zero, otherwise monthlyEssentials. Cash after = cash − the shock. Months of cover after the shock = cash after (never below 0) ÷ essentials. Months of cover with no shock = cash ÷ essentials. Both are 0 when essentials are 0. Covers it when cash after is zero or more. Recommended fund = essentials × 3. Gap = recommended fund − cash, never below 0.

MK-CF-F-011.name: savingsByMonth
MK-CF-F-011.rule: For each calendar month: the take-home that month (incomeMonthlyGrid, take-home) − the planned expenses that month (spendByMonth).

MK-CF-F-012.name: annualCashflow
MK-CF-F-012.rule: Gross for the year, after-tax for the year and take-home for the year = the twelve months of incomeMonthlyGrid in each of its three modes, added. Expenses for the year = spendByMonth added. Tax = gross − after-tax. 401(k) = after-tax − take-home. Saved = take-home − expenses.

MK-CF-F-013.name: budgetFromOnboarding
MK-CF-F-013.rule: The stored budget: monthly expenses = plannedMonthlySpend; fixed, non-monthly and flexible from spendBuckets.

MK-CF-F-014.name: budgetVsActual
MK-CF-F-014.rule: This calendar month's logged expenses, leaving out the category Debt payment, added into fixed, non-monthly or flexible by each expense's category. For each bucket: planned (spendBuckets), spent, remaining = planned − spent. The totals the same way.

MK-CF-F-017.name: publishSurplus
MK-CF-F-017.rule: Announces the projected-to-save figure to the rest of the app, unchanged.

MK-CF-F-018.name: equityByMonth
MK-CF-F-018.rule: Each vesting row's value (equityRowValue) goes to the month in its date — December when it has no date. The year's vesting (rsuAnnual) is then split across the twelve months in proportion to those values. All zero when no row has a value.

MK-CF-F-019.name: upcomingBills
MK-CF-F-019.rule: Bills = each non-monthly budget category, once for every month it names (January when it names none): amount = its yearly amount ÷ the number of months named (a percent one = percent × monthly income after tax × 12), on its due day (the 1st when none), at its next date on or after today. Only bills due from today to the horizon (365 days when none is given) are returned, soonest first. Need-by date = due date − 2 days; ask-by date = need-by − 10 days. Money available by the need-by date = starting balance + steady daily net × the days from today + one-off inflows (yearly scholarships, loans) dated on or before it − other bills dated on or before it. Steady daily net = (steady monthly in − steady monthly out) × 12 ÷ 365. Steady in = the LARGEST month of gross salary, tips, retirement income and net rent ÷ 12, each × (1 − the rate in force), plus support, benefits for the year ÷ 12 and monthly scholarships untaxed. Steady out = fixed + flexible budget + the part of the typed monthly figure above the categories. Shortfall = bill − available, never below 0.

MK-CF-F-020.name: cashflowYear
MK-CF-F-020.rule: Twelve months starting with the current one. Taxed income each month = that calendar month's gross salary + tips (only in months with salary) + self-employment + net rent ÷ 12 + interest and dividends ÷ 12 + other income when taxable + that month's stock vesting + retirement income; plus the bonus in its month (December when none is set); a signing bonus in the first month; one-off other income in its month. Untaxed = benefits in their months + support + untaxed other income + scholarships (monthly, or in their months, or ÷ 12 when they name none) + loans in their months (the first month when they name none). Inflow = taxed × (1 − the rate in force) + untaxed. Outflow = the planned expenses for that calendar month (spendByMonth). The balance starts at the starting balance and each month adds inflow − outflow. Short months = those ending below zero. Lowest balance = the smallest month-end. Dated items that fall outside the twelve months are counted, not included.

MK-CF-F-021.name: defaultPaymentType
MK-CF-F-021.rule: A credit card or a home-equity line: revolving. Every other kind of debt: instalment.

MK-CF-F-022.name: paymentShape
MK-CF-F-022.rule: The payment type recorded on the debt; when none is recorded, defaultPaymentType.

MK-CF-F-023.name: requiredPayment
MK-CF-F-023.rule: 0 for a debt due in full. Otherwise the larger of the minimum monthly payment and the payment the person says they make.

MK-CF-F-025.name: minimumDebtService
MK-CF-F-025.rule: Each debt's minimum monthly payment added; a debt due in full counts 0.

MK-CF-F-026.name: actualDebtPayment
MK-CF-F-026.rule: The same as totalDebtMonthly: requiredPayment added over the debts.

MK-CF-F-028.name: loanPayment
MK-CF-F-028.rule: Months = years × 12, rounded to a whole number; monthly rate = the yearly percent ÷ 100 ÷ 12. All zero when the amount borrowed or the months are zero or less. Payment = amount × monthly rate ÷ (1 − (1 + monthly rate) to the power −months); with no interest, amount ÷ months. Total paid = payment × months. Total interest = total paid − amount.

MK-CF-F-029.name: monthsToClear
MK-CF-F-029.rule: 0 when nothing is owed. No answer when the payment is zero or less, or when it does not exceed the first month's interest (balance × yearly rate ÷ 12) — the debt would never clear. With no interest: balance ÷ payment, rounded up. Otherwise log(payment ÷ (payment − balance × monthly rate)) ÷ log(1 + monthly rate), rounded up to a whole month.

MK-CF-F-030.name: paymentToClearBy
MK-CF-F-030.rule: 0 when nothing is owed or the months are zero or less. Payment = balance × monthly rate ÷ (1 − (1 + monthly rate) to the power −months), monthly rate = yearly rate ÷ 12; with no interest, balance ÷ months. Rounded UP to the cent.

MK-CF-F-031.name: creditUtilization
MK-CF-F-031.rule: Share = balance ÷ limit (0 when the limit is zero or less). Good at 30% or under; caution above 30% up to 50%; high above 50% — judged before rounding. The share is then rounded to three decimals.

MK-CF-F-032.name: creditScoreBand
MK-CF-F-032.rule: 800 and above Excellent; 740 and above Very good; 670 and above Good; 580 and above Fair; below 580 Poor. Good, Very good and Excellent count as good.

MK-CF-F-033.name: debtToIncome
MK-CF-F-033.rule: Share = monthly debt payments ÷ monthly gross income (0 when the income is zero or less). Guideline: 36% for a homeowner, 20% otherwise. Good at or under the guideline; caution up to 1.4 × the guideline (50.4% for a homeowner, 28% otherwise); high above that. The share is rounded to three decimals after it is judged.

MK-CF-F-034.name: payoffPlan
MK-CF-F-034.rule: Only debts with a balance above zero. A debt due in full is paid in its due month (never earlier than month 1; month 1 when it has no date), with interest = balance × ((1 + yearly rate ÷ 12) to the power of the months until then − 1). The others are walked month by month, for at most 600 months. Each month: every balance grows by balance × yearly rate ÷ 12; the money to pay = the minimums of every debt whose payments have started — including debts already cleared, whose minimums roll on — plus the extra; each debt first gets its minimum (never more than it owes); what is left goes to one debt at a time, highest rate first (avalanche) or smallest balance first (snowball). A debt is cleared when it owes a cent or less. A debt whose first payment date is in the future is not paid until that month, and grows meanwhile. Months = the month the last debt is cleared (or the last lump-sum month, when later); total interest = all the interest charged; it never pays off when anything is still owed at month 600. Order = each debt with the month it is cleared and the interest it cost, earliest first.

MK-CF-F-035.name: debtKind
MK-CF-F-035.rule: The label and icon recorded for a kind of debt; nothing for a kind that is not on the list.

MK-CF-F-036.name: buildDebtState
MK-CF-F-036.rule: Total = the balances that are known, added (totalDebtBalance) — a debt with no balance is left out, not counted as zero. Minimum in a month = minimumDebtService. Actual payment in a month = actualDebtPayment. Highest-rate debt = the one with the largest yearly rate, the first of equals. High-cost debt = the balances of the debts whose rate is ABOVE 7%, added.

MK-CF-F-037.name: inferDebtType
MK-CF-F-037.rule: From the debt's name, capitals ignored, first match wins: heloc or home equity → home-equity line; mortgage or home loan → mortgage; auto, car loan or vehicle → auto; student or tuition → student loan; credit card, visa, mastercard or amex → credit card; medical, hospital or dental → medical; personal → personal; anything else → other.

MK-CF-F-038.name: debtsFromOnboarding
MK-CF-F-038.rule: One debt when the balance entered at sign-up is above zero: its name (Debt when blank), its kind from the name (inferDebtType), the balance, yearly rate = the percent entered ÷ 100, and the minimum payment. None otherwise.

MK-CF-F-041.name: getDebtState
MK-CF-F-041.rule: Loads the stored debts and gives buildDebtState of them; nothing when none are stored.

MK-CF-F-042.name: mortgageOddsEffect
MK-CF-F-042.rule: Nothing when the extra is zero or less, or when the mortgage would never clear at either payment (monthsToClear). Payoff year = this year + the whole years in (months − 1) ÷ 12 — worked for the present payment and for payment + extra. Before = the retirement projection's chance of success with the present payment running through its payoff year. After = the chance with payment + extra running through the earlier payoff year, the yearly saving lowered by extra × 12 until then, and raised by (payment + extra) × 12 from the year after.

MK-CF-F-043.name: compareMortgageToTreasury
MK-CF-F-043.rule: Nothing unless the balance, the rate and the payment are all above zero. Gap = (mortgage rate − Treasury yield) in percentage points, to two decimals. Too close to call when the gap is under 0.25 points either way; otherwise paying down wins when the gap is positive and Treasuries win when it is negative. Yearly difference = (mortgage rate − Treasury yield) × balance. Lifetime difference — only with an extra above zero and a mortgage that clears both ways — = what (payment + extra) a month grows to at the Treasury yield over the months freed by clearing early, minus what the extra a month grows to at the Treasury yield over all the months the mortgage would otherwise run (futureValue, amortise).

MK-CF-F-044.name: annualNet
MK-CF-F-044.rule: The amount each period — for rent, rent less running costs each period — × the periods in a year: weekly 52, every two weeks 26, monthly 12, quarterly 4, yearly 1, one-off 1.

MK-CF-F-046.name: employerMatchAnnual
MK-CF-F-046.rule: Each source's employer match each period × its periods in a year, added.

MK-CF-F-048.name: effectiveTaxRate
MK-CF-F-048.rule: With the person's own rate switched on: that rate, held between 0 and 1. Otherwise federal income tax on the yearly gross ÷ the yearly gross, by filing status (single when none), with no state tax (effectiveRateOnGrossFor).

MK-CF-F-049.name: buildIncomeState
MK-CF-F-049.rule: Yearly gross = grossAnnualBaseline. Rate = effectiveTaxRate. Yearly after-tax = gross × (1 − rate); monthly after-tax = that ÷ 12. Month grid: each source's gross laid on the calendar (monthlyGrossOfSource), added by month. Tax each month = that month's gross × the rate, when the person's own rate is on; otherwise the federal tax on the year's running total up to and including that month, minus the tax up to the month before — worked AS A SINGLE FILER, with no state tax. After-tax that month = gross − tax. Employer match for the year = employerMatchAnnual.

MK-CF-F-052.name: getIncomeState
MK-CF-F-052.rule: Loads the stored income and gives buildIncomeState of it; nothing when none is stored.

MK-CF-F-053.name: annual401kLimit
MK-CF-F-053.rule: 2026: $24,500. At age 50 or over, + $8,000. Ages 60 to 63 get + $11,250 INSTEAD of the $8,000. So $32,500 at ages 50 to 59 and from 64 on, and $35,750 at 60 to 63. With no age: $24,500.

MK-CF-F-054.name: annualIraLimit
MK-CF-F-054.rule: 2026: $7,500; + $1,100 at age 50 or over. With no age: $7,500.

MK-CF-F-055.name: annualHsaLimit
MK-CF-F-055.rule: 0 when enrolled in Medicare. Otherwise, 2026: $4,400 for self-only cover or $8,750 for family cover; + $1,000 at age 55 or over.

MK-CF-F-056.name: k401Headroom
MK-CF-F-056.rule: Limit = annual401kLimit. Used = the year's contribution (below zero counts 0), never more than the limit. Room = limit − the contribution, never below 0. Catch-up flag at 50 or over.

MK-CF-F-057.name: rothVsTraditional
MK-CF-F-057.rule: Top tax band now at 12% or under: lean Roth. Band now at 24% or over AND the band expected in retirement lower than now: lean Traditional. Anything else: either.

MK-CF-F-058.name: rothConversionWindow
MK-CF-F-058.rule: True when the age is at or past the retirement age AND below the earlier of age 73 and the Social Security claiming age (73 when there is no claiming age).

MK-CF-F-059.name: annualizedEnteredSalary
MK-CF-F-059.rule: Hourly: base pay × hours a week (40 when none) × 52. Otherwise base pay × the periods in a year: weekly 52, every two weeks 26, monthly 12, yearly 1 — monthly when no frequency is given.

MK-CF-F-060.name: salaryGrossByMonth
MK-CF-F-060.rule: Each earner's twelve months of gross pay (wageGrossByMonth), added month by month.

MK-CF-F-061.name: grossSalaryMonthly
MK-CF-F-061.rule: The LARGEST of the twelve monthly gross salary figures (salaryGrossByMonth).

MK-CF-F-062.name: equityRowValue
MK-CF-F-062.rule: An option: shares × (market price − strike price), never below 0. Any other grant: shares × price.

MK-CF-F-063.name: rowVestYear
MK-CF-F-063.rule: The first four-digit year in the row's date; this year when it has none.

MK-CF-F-064.name: equityCashFlow
MK-CF-F-064.rule: The value of each vesting row (equityRowValue) added by vesting year; rows of zero or less are left out; earliest year first.

MK-CF-F-065.name: equityVestWeights
MK-CF-F-065.rule: Each row's value goes to the month in its date (December when it has none); each month's share = its value ÷ the total. Nothing when no row has a value.

MK-CF-F-066.name: rsuAnnual
MK-CF-F-066.rule: With vesting rows: their total value ÷ the number of different years in which rows with a value vest (at least 1). With none: shares × price, as typed.

MK-CF-F-067.name: rentalList
MK-CF-F-067.rule: Each rent entry that names its property (a property identifier that is not blank) with rent or running costs above zero: long-term unless marked short-term, its monthly rent and its monthly running costs. An entry that names no property is not counted (owner rule DEC-4059d, 2026-10-10). With no list of rent entries: nothing — the old single typed rent figure names no property, so it is not counted either. Owner rule, 2026-10-10: each rent and running-cost figure is read only when it is a plain number (digits with at most one decimal point, allowing a leading dollar sign, thousands commas and spaces); a figure with letters or other text in it is not entered and counts as 0, never as the digits inside it.

figures_checked_by_hand.4059: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-4059d (2026-10-10) that this rule follows

MK-CF-F-068.name: rentalNetAnnual
MK-CF-F-068.rule: (Monthly rent − monthly running costs) added over the rentals, × 12. A rental that loses money pulls the total down.

MK-CF-F-069.name: benefitActiveMonths
MK-CF-F-069.rule: The months, 1 to 12, in which the benefit is paid, in order; all twelve when none are named.

MK-CF-F-070.name: benefitAnnual
MK-CF-F-070.rule: The monthly benefit × the number of months it is paid (benefitActiveMonths).

MK-CF-F-071.name: extraIncome
MK-CF-F-071.rule: Taxed in a month = self-employment (yearly ÷ 12, or the monthly figure) + interest and dividends ÷ 12 + other income when taxable (yearly ÷ 12, or the monthly figure). Untaxed in a month = benefits for the year ÷ 12 + support + scholarships (monthly, or yearly ÷ 12) + other income when marked not taxable. One-off other income goes to one-off taxed or one-off untaxed. Reinvested in a month = interest and dividends ÷ 12, unless they are paid to the bank — then 0.

MK-CF-F-072.name: currentRetirementIncomeMonthly
MK-CF-F-072.rule: 0 when the person's chosen income sources are listed and retirement income is not among them; otherwise retirementIncomeMonthly.

MK-CF-F-073.name: otherIncomeMonth
MK-CF-F-073.rule: The month typed for the other income, held between 1 and 12; January when none.

MK-CF-F-074.name: tipsAnnual
MK-CF-F-074.rule: Monthly tips × the number of months with any salary (salaryActiveMonths).

MK-CF-F-075.name: retirementIncomeMonthly
MK-CF-F-075.rule: Social Security, pension, withdrawals, required distributions, annuities and other, each turned into a month — monthly as it is, quarterly ÷ 3, yearly ÷ 12 — and added.

MK-CF-F-076.name: guaranteedOutsideStreams
MK-CF-F-076.rule: Social Security, pension, annuity and other, each as a monthly amount (quarterly ÷ 3, yearly ÷ 12), only those above zero. Rises with prices: Social Security yes, the others no — unless the person said otherwise. Withdrawals and required distributions are not here.

MK-CF-F-077.name: scholarshipByCalendarMonth
MK-CF-F-077.rule: Twelve months. A monthly scholarship adds its amount every month. A yearly one is split evenly over the months it names, or over all twelve when it names none. With no list: the single typed amount — monthly, or ÷ 12.

MK-CF-F-078.name: employerMatchMonthly
MK-CF-F-078.rule: Each earner's match in a month (wageMatchMonthly), added.

MK-CF-F-079.name: incomeFromOnboarding
MK-CF-F-079.rule: Builds the stored income list from the sign-up answers, one source for each amount above zero: base salary = yearly salary ÷ 12, monthly, with the employer match; the bonus, yearly, in its month (December when none); stock vesting, yearly, split by vesting month; a signing bonus, once, in January; each rental, monthly, with its running costs; tips = yearly tips ÷ 12, monthly; retirement income, monthly; self-employment, monthly or yearly; interest and dividends, yearly; benefits = the year ÷ 12, monthly; support, monthly; each scholarship; other income with its frequency and month. Tax: the person's own rate (percent ÷ 100, held between 0 and 1) when they chose to type one; otherwise calculated.

MK-CF-F-080.name: jobActiveMonth
MK-CF-F-080.rule: True when that calendar month's gross salary is above zero.

MK-CF-F-081.name: salaryActiveMonths
MK-CF-F-081.rule: How many of the twelve months have gross salary above zero.

MK-CF-F-082.name: salaryAnnual
MK-CF-F-082.rule: The twelve months of gross salary (salaryGrossByMonth) added.

MK-CF-F-083.name: totalGrossAnnual
MK-CF-F-083.rule: Salary for the year + tips for the year + bonus + signing bonus + stock vesting + net rent + taxed extra in a month × 12 + untaxed extra in a month × 12 + one-off taxed + one-off untaxed + retirement income in a month × 12.

MK-CF-F-084.name: taxableAnnual
MK-CF-F-084.rule: totalGrossAnnual WITHOUT the untaxed parts: salary + tips + bonus + signing bonus + stock vesting + net rent + taxed extra in a month × 12 + one-off taxed + retirement income in a month × 12. The 401(k) is NOT taken off here.

MK-CF-F-085.name: filingStatusOf
MK-CF-F-085.rule: The filing status the person chose: married, married filing separately or head of household; anything else, single. When none is chosen: married when there is a spouse or the spouse earns; single otherwise.

MK-CF-F-086.name: stateRateOf
MK-CF-F-086.rule: The state rate typed, as a percent ÷ 100, held between 0 and 15%.

MK-CF-F-087.name: monthlyTaxRates
MK-CF-F-087.rule: Twelve rates, all the same: the rate in force (rateInForce) — the person's own, or the calculated one. A steady income is taxed the same in every month.

MK-CF-F-088.name: taxableByCalendarMonth
MK-CF-F-088.rule: For each calendar month: gross salary + tips (only in months with salary) + net rent ÷ 12 + that month's stock vesting + taxed extra in a month + retirement income; + the bonus in its month (December when none); + the signing bonus in January; + one-off taxed other income in its month; − the household's 401(k) that month. Never below 0.

MK-CF-F-089.name: over65CountOf
MK-CF-F-089.rule: Married filing jointly with the question answered: both → 2, neither → 0, one → 1. Otherwise from the person's own birth year: 1 when this year − birth year is 65 or more, else 0; 0 with no birth year.

MK-CF-F-091.name: userCapGainsRates
MK-CF-F-091.rule: On the household's total yearly income (totalGrossAnnual), by filing status: long-term rate = the federal long-term gains rate (0%, 15% or 20%) + the state rate; short-term rate = the top federal band + the state rate.

MK-CF-F-092.name: incomeMonthlyGrid
MK-CF-F-092.rule: For each calendar month. Earned before 401(k) = that month's taxed income (taxableByCalendarMonth) + that month's 401(k). Untaxed = support + that month's scholarships + benefits in their months + one-off untaxed income in its month. Gross = earned before 401(k) + untaxed − reinvested interest and dividends. Tax = tax on the wages + tax on the rest. The wages, earner by earner: an earner who typed a take-home is taxed at their own share — (their yearly gross − their 401(k) for the year − 12 × the typed take-home) ÷ their yearly gross, held between 0 and 1 — so they land exactly what they typed; any other earner's wage × the rate in force (monthlyTaxRates). The rest (earned before 401(k) − the wages) × the rate in force — except that when the rate is the person's own, the month's rent and interest and dividends are left out, because they are not on a payslip. After-tax = gross − tax. Take-home = gross − tax − 401(k).

MK-CF-F-097.name: grossFromNet
MK-CF-F-097.rule: 0 when the take-home is zero or less. Otherwise it searches between the take-home and three times it, halving the range 50 times, for the gross at which gross − federal tax (taxOwedFor, no state tax) equals the take-home.

MK-CF-F-098.name: progressiveMonthlyTax
MK-CF-F-098.rule: For each month in order: the federal tax on the year's running total up to and including that month − the federal tax on the running total before it; plus state tax = the rise in taxable income over the same step × the state rate (held between 0 and 15%). A negative month counts 0.

MK-CF-F-099.name: deductionFor
MK-CF-F-099.rule: The standard deduction for the filing status + the age-65 addition × the number of people 65 or over (2 at most) + the senior deduction (seniorDeductionFor). The amounts are in the 2026 table above the cards.

MK-CF-F-100.name: taxableIncomeFor
MK-CF-F-100.rule: Gross − the deduction (deductionFor, with the gross itself used as the income for the senior deduction's phase-out); never below 0.

MK-CF-F-101.name: taxOwedFor
MK-CF-F-101.rule: Taxable income (taxableIncomeFor) taxed band by band on the filing status's 2026 table — each slice at its own rate — plus taxable income × the state rate (held between 0 and 15%).

MK-CF-F-102.name: effectiveRateOnGrossFor
MK-CF-F-102.rule: taxOwedFor ÷ gross; 0 when the gross is zero or less.

MK-CF-F-103.name: marginalBracketFor
MK-CF-F-103.rule: The rate of the band the taxable income falls in; income exactly on a band's top belongs to that band.

MK-CF-F-104.name: ltcgRateFor
MK-CF-F-104.rule: On taxable income (taxableIncomeFor): 0% up to the first threshold, 15% up to the second, 20% above. 2026 thresholds — single $49,450 and $545,500; married $98,900 and $613,700; married filing separately $49,450 and $306,850; head of household $66,200 and $579,600. Income exactly on a threshold takes the lower rate.

MK-CF-F-105.name: guaranteedRows
MK-CF-F-105.rule: Nothing when the person's chosen income sources are listed without retirement income. Otherwise, over the twelve months starting with the current one, for Social Security, pension, annuity and other retirement income with an amount above zero: monthly → the amount in every month; quarterly → the amount in four months, three apart, starting at its named month (the current month when none); yearly → the amount once, in its named month (the current month when none). The amount is the amount of EACH PAYMENT.

MK-CF-F-106.name: solveSafeDraw
MK-CF-F-106.rule: 0 when the savings are zero or less. Otherwise the largest monthly draw from the savings, on top of the guaranteed income, at which the retirement simulation (1,000 futures, fixed seed 42) still lasts to the horizon in at least 80 of 100. It is tried first at twice (savings ÷ years ÷ 12), $100 at least; then narrowed by halving 12 times; then rounded DOWN to the nearest $5.

MK-CF-F-107.name: buildPaycheckYear
MK-CF-F-107.rule: Guaranteed rows from guaranteedRows; savings = the figure given, otherwise the accounts set aside for retirement. Safe draw = solveSafeDraw, with average guaranteed income in a month = the rows' total ÷ 12. Draw flag: high when safe draw × 12 ÷ savings is above 4.5%; ok otherwise; none with no savings or no draw. For each of twelve months from the current one: guaranteed total = that month's rows; bills = that month's big bills, everyday expenses left out; safe to spend = guaranteed total + safe draw − bills. This year = the twelve added.

MK-CF-F-108.name: isMoneyOut
MK-CF-F-108.rule: True for a withdrawal, a fee, or a transfer with no receiving account on record.

MK-CF-F-109.name: reviewTransactions
MK-CF-F-109.rule: Flags, in this order; a record is flagged once. (1) Possible duplicate — any new money-out above zero that has an earlier one on the same account with the same amount (within half a cent) and the same payee, 2 days apart or less. (2) For money-out from a LINKED account only — unusually large: with 5 or more money-outs on that account within 90 days of it, at least 3 × their middle value AND at least $500; with fewer than 5, at least $1,000. (3) Otherwise first-time payee — a payee not seen on that account in those 90 days and not on the known list, for $250 or more. (4) Odd pattern — 3 or more money-outs from one account on one day (the new unflagged ones plus earlier ones that day) adding to $1,000 or more.

MK-CF-F-110.name: flagComparisonText
MK-CF-F-110.rule: The sentence for a flag. Unusually large, with a typical figure: it names the typical amount in whole dollars and how many times larger this one is, rounded to a whole number; with none: it says anything over $1,000 is looked at twice. First-time payee and possible duplicate each have a fixed sentence. Several in one day: it names how many and their total in whole dollars.

MK-CF-F-111.name: applyTransaction
MK-CF-F-111.rule: What one record does to the accounts. Adjustment: nothing. Opening position: adds the shares at their price as a purchase. Opening cash: sets the account's cash to the amount. Deposit: cash up by the amount. Withdrawal or fee: cash down by the amount. Buy: cash down by shares × price, and the shares added as a purchase. Sale with shares: sells at most the shares held (when a purchase has no share count, so the shares held are unknown, the sale stands as recorded) — cash up by the shares sold × price, earliest purchases reduced first; a sale with no shares but an amount lowers the balance by the amount, never below 0. Transfer: cash down on the sending account, and up on the receiving one when there is one. Transfer of a holding: the whole holding moves to the other account. Dividend, interest or coupon: when reinvested with shares and a price, a purchase is added to a holding already there; otherwise cash up by the amount.

MK-CF-F-112.name: makeTransaction
MK-CF-F-112.rule: The record as given, with its ticker in capitals, a new id and the time it was made.

MK-CF-F-113.name: affectedAccountIds
MK-CF-F-113.rule: The record's account, and the receiving account when there is one.

MK-CF-F-114.name: undoSnapshot
MK-CF-F-114.rule: A full copy of each account the record touches, as it stands before the record is applied.

MK-CF-F-115.name: restoreUndo
MK-CF-F-115.rule: Each account the record touched is put back to the copy saved with it; the other accounts are unchanged.

MK-CF-F-116.name: inverseOf
MK-CF-F-116.rule: The record that undoes one. A deposit → a withdrawal; a withdrawal or a fee → a deposit; a transfer between two accounts → the same transfer the other way; a transfer out with no receiving account → a deposit; a dividend, interest or coupon paid in cash → a withdrawal; an adjustment → itself. Nothing for a buy, a sale, an opening record, a transfer of a holding or a reinvested payment.

MK-CF-F-117.name: txnLabel
MK-CF-F-117.rule: The plain name for a kind of record; the kind's own code when it has none.

MK-CF-F-118.name: cashEffect
MK-CF-F-118.rule: The change in cash from one record. Deposit: + amount. Sale: + shares × price — the amount, when that product is zero. Dividend, interest, coupon: + amount; 0 when reinvested. Withdrawal or fee: − amount. Buy: − shares × price. Transfer: − amount. Anything else: 0.

MK-CF-F-119.name: investmentIncomeAnnual
MK-CF-F-119.rule: Dividends, interest and coupons dated within the last year (on or after the same date a year ago), not reinvested, added.

MK-CF-F-120.name: pctBaseMonthly
MK-CF-F-120.rule: The twelve months of take-home (incomeMonthlyGrid, take-home) added ÷ 12.

MK-CF-F-122.name: addDays
MK-CF-F-122.rule: The date moved by that many whole days.

MK-CF-F-124.name: nextOccurrence
MK-CF-F-124.rule: With a year given: that month and day in that year. Otherwise that month and day (the 1st when no day) this year — or next year, when this year's date is already before now.

MK-CF-F-125.name: amortise
MK-CF-F-125.rule: Never clears — infinite months and interest — when the payment does not exceed the first month's interest. Otherwise month by month, for at most 1,200: interest = balance × yearly rate ÷ 12; balance = balance + interest − payment; until the balance is zero or less. Gives the months, and the interest added up.

MK-CF-F-126.name: futureValue
MK-CF-F-126.rule: 0 when the months or the monthly amount are zero or less. Otherwise monthly amount × ((1 + yearly rate ÷ 12) to the power months − 1) ÷ (yearly rate ÷ 12).

MK-CF-F-127.name: isRental
MK-CF-F-127.rule: True for a long-term rental or a short-term rental.

MK-CF-F-128.name: grossByMonth
MK-CF-F-128.rule: When the pay varies and a month-by-month table has been filled: the table, one row a month, in month order. Otherwise one row, called typical = the typical gross pay turned into a month (perMonth).

MK-CF-F-130.name: enteredMonthlyRaw
MK-CF-F-130.rule: Hourly: base pay × hours a week (40 when none) × 52 ÷ 12. Otherwise base pay × the periods in a year ÷ 12 (weekly 52, every two weeks 26, monthly 12, yearly 1).

MK-CF-F-131.name: normPayee
MK-CF-F-131.rule: The payee note trimmed and lower-cased; empty when there is none.

MK-CF-F-132.name: map
MK-CF-F-132.rule: The list of accounts with one change applied to the account named, and the rest untouched.

MK-CF-F-133.name: cashOf
MK-CF-F-133.rule: The account's cash; 0 when none is recorded.

MK-CF-F-134.name: usesSleeve
MK-CF-F-134.rule: True for an investment account (not a cash or property account) whose balance is worked out from its holdings, or that records a cash figure of its own.

MK-CF-F-135.name: availableCash
MK-CF-F-135.rule: For such an account (usesSleeve): its cash. For any other: its balance.

MK-CF-F-136.name: bumpCash
MK-CF-F-136.rule: For an account that keeps its own cash (usesSleeve): the cash changes by the amount. For an investment account with holdings that does not: both the cash and the balance change by the amount. For any other account: the balance changes by the amount.

MK-CF-F-137.name: findPos
MK-CF-F-137.rule: The holding in the account with the record's holding id, or else with the record's ticker (the record's ticker read in capitals).

MK-CF-F-138.name: addLot
MK-CF-F-138.rule: Adds a purchase (shares, cost per share, the record's date) to the holding the record names; when the account has no such holding, a new holding with that one purchase.

MK-CF-F-139.name: removeShares
MK-CF-F-139.rule: Takes the shares out of the holding's purchases oldest purchase date first (a purchase with no date goes last), whatever order they are stored in; a purchase left with nothing is dropped; a holding left with no purchases is removed. Unchanged when the account has no such holding.

MK-CF-F-140.name: periodsAYear
MK-CF-F-140.rule: Pay periods in a year: hourly 2,080, weekly 52, every two weeks 26, monthly 12, yearly 1. Any other frequency: 12.

MK-CF-F-141.name: perMonth
MK-CF-F-141.rule: Hourly: amount × hours a week (40 when none is entered) × 52 ÷ 12. Any other frequency: amount × pay periods in a year ÷ 12.

MK-CF-F-142.name: monthsOf
MK-CF-F-142.rule: The table's rows as (month, amount) pairs, sorted by month; a blank amount counts as 0; empty when there is no table.

MK-CF-F-143.name: annualisedGross
MK-CF-F-143.rule: The average of the monthly gross rows (grossByMonth) × 12. 0 when there are no rows.

MK-CF-F-144.name: takeHomeAsEntered
MK-CF-F-144.rule: In this order. (1) The pay varies and a month-by-month take-home table is filled: the average of its months; not calculated. (2) A take-home above zero was typed: that amount exactly as typed — it is asked for as a MONTH, whatever the pay frequency; not calculated. (3) Otherwise it is calculated, and marked so. With a household rate supplied: (yearly gross × (1 − rate) − monthly 401(k) × 12) ÷ 12. With none: (yearly gross − 401(k) for the year − federal income tax on the yearly gross less the 401(k), by the filing status given — single when none) ÷ 12. That federal tax has no state tax in it.

MK-CF-F-145.name: deductionsFromPay
MK-CF-F-145.rule: Nothing when the take-home is calculated. Otherwise yearly gross − monthly 401(k) × 12 − monthly take-home × 12: everything else that came out of pay in the year.

MK-CF-F-146.name: payFiguresAgree
MK-CF-F-146.rule: It passes with no check when the take-home is calculated. Otherwise, for each month of gross pay in order: left = gross − monthly 401(k) − the take-home for that month (the month's own figure when a take-home table is filled, otherwise the typed take-home, which is a monthly figure at every pay frequency). When left is below −$5: it FAILS, with a sentence naming the month and how much more the take-home is than there is. Otherwise, when gross is above zero and left ÷ gross is above 60%: it passes WITH A WARNING that gives that share as a whole percent. The first month to fail or warn decides. Exactly $5 short still passes; exactly 60% does not warn.

MK-CF-F-148.name: inMonth
MK-CF-F-148.rule: True when the expense's date begins with the year-month asked for.

MK-CF-F-149.name: recurringDebtPayments
MK-CF-F-149.rule: One row for each debt whose payment is the same every month (an instalment loan): its name and its required monthly payment (requiredPayment). Rows of zero are dropped. Cards, lines of credit and debts due in full are not here.

MK-CF-F-150.name: debtPaymentsCountedAsExpenses
MK-CF-F-150.rule: For each debt that is NOT an instalment loan, and whose purchases are not already imported from a linked card: the payments logged this month under the category Debt payment whose payee matches the debt's name (capitals and outer spaces ignored), added up. A row only when that is above zero, named after the debt with the word payment.

MK-CF-F-151.name: actualSpending
MK-CF-F-151.rule: The month's logged expenses, leaving out the category Debt payment, newest first — all of them, or only those entered by hand, or only those imported. Shown = the first 5. Hidden = how many more. Total = all of them added. Hidden total = total − the 5 shown.

MK-CF-F-152.name: isRadarItem
MK-CF-F-152.rule: An instalment loan: not a radar item. A debt due in full: a lump-sum item. Any other debt (a card, a line of credit): a revolving item.

MK-CF-F-153.name: radar
MK-CF-F-153.rule: For each debt that is a radar item (isRadarItem): amount = what was logged as paid against it this month when that is above zero, otherwise its required payment; dropped when the amount is zero or less. It counts as an expense unless its purchases are already imported from a linked card. Then every big bill of $500 or more, with its due date, each counted as an expense. Debts first, bills after.

MK-CF-F-155.name: cash
MK-CF-F-155.rule: The number unchanged, except that negative zero becomes zero.

MK-CF-F-156.name: plannedMonthFlow
MK-CF-F-156.rule: Rows, in this order. Inflow = the monthly take-home handed in. One row for each instalment debt with a required payment above zero: minus that payment. Expenses = minus the budget when one is set (above zero); otherwise 0, marked not set. Then one row for each radar debt (a card, a line of credit) with a required payment above zero: minus that payment. Surplus = every row added up.

MK-CF-F-157.name: debtPaymentsByDebt
MK-CF-F-157.rule: For each expense logged this month in the category Debt payment whose payee matches a debt's name (capitals and outer spaces ignored): its amount is added to that debt. Payments that match no debt are left out.

MK-CF-F-160.name: daysBetweenDates
MK-CF-F-160.rule: The second date − the first, in days, rounded to the nearest whole day.

MK-CF-F-161.name: monthlyGrossOfSource
MK-CF-F-161.rule: Twelve calendar months; rent is taken after running costs. Monthly: the amount every month. Weekly: amount × 52 ÷ 12 every month. Every two weeks: amount × 26 ÷ 12 every month. Quarterly: the amount in March, June, September and December. Yearly: the amount in its month (December when none) — or split across its months by their shares. One-off: the amount in its month (January when none).

MK-CF-F-162.name: daysApart
MK-CF-F-162.rule: The gap between two dates in days, never negative.

MK-CF-F-163.name: monthKey
MK-CF-F-163.rule: A date written as year-month, for example 2026-08.

MK-CF-F-164.name: monthWindow
MK-CF-F-164.rule: A run of year-months: it starts that many months back from the given date and holds that many months.

MK-CF-F-165.name: salaryMonths
MK-CF-F-165.rule: The stored month table as year-month → amount. A table kept as twelve plain figures is read as January to December of this year. Rows whose key is not a year-month are dropped. Empty when there is none.

MK-CF-F-166.name: hasMonthlySalaryTable
MK-CF-F-166.rule: True when salaryMonths holds any row.

MK-CF-F-167.name: salaryCalendarYear
MK-CF-F-167.rule: January to December of the year asked for: the table's figure where it has that month, otherwise the fallback.

MK-CF-F-168.name: salaryWindow
MK-CF-F-168.rule: For each year-month asked for: the table's figure where it has it, otherwise the fallback.

MK-CF-F-169.name: withSalaryMonth
MK-CF-F-169.rule: The table with that one month set to the amount (a blank counts 0); every other month unchanged.

MK-CF-F-170.name: salaryYearFromCells
MK-CF-F-170.rule: The first twelve figures, as January to December of the year given.

MK-CF-F-171.name: earnerPay
MK-CF-F-171.rule: One earner's pay figures together: gross in a month = yearly gross ÷ 12; yearly gross (annualisedGross); the monthly 401(k); the take-home, whether it is calculated and why (takeHomeAsEntered); everything else taken out, for the year and ÷ 12 for the month — nothing when the take-home is calculated; the verdict (payFiguresAgree); and the monthly gross rows.

MK-CF-F-172.name: hasWage
MK-CF-F-172.rule: True when a wage record has a base salary above zero, or a month table with any row.

MK-CF-F-173.name: earnerWages
MK-CF-F-173.rule: Who earns = both: the person's own wage record, plus the spouse's when it has a wage. Who earns = the spouse, and the spouse's record has a wage: the spouse's only. Otherwise the person's own only.

MK-CF-F-174.name: hasTwoEarners
MK-CF-F-174.rule: True when earnerWages gives more than one.

MK-CF-F-175.name: sumOverEarners
MK-CF-F-175.rule: The chosen figure worked for each earner and added; a missing figure counts 0.

MK-CF-F-176.name: sumMonthsOverEarners
MK-CF-F-176.rule: The chosen twelve-month row worked for each earner and added month by month.

MK-CF-F-177.name: wageGrossByMonth
MK-CF-F-177.rule: With a month table: this calendar year's twelve months from the table, any month not in it taking the typical monthly figure. With none: the typical monthly figure (enteredMonthlyRaw) in every month.

MK-CF-F-178.name: wageMatchMonthly
MK-CF-F-178.rule: A match typed as a percent: monthly 401(k) × that percent ÷ 100. Typed as dollars: that amount.

MK-CF-F-179.name: entryFromWage
MK-CF-F-179.rule: Turns a stored wage record into the pay entry: frequency (monthly when none); varies = the record says month-by-month, or its month table holds any row; typical gross = the base salary; the month table, only when it varies; the monthly 401(k); the typed take-home; hours a week.

MK-CF-F-180.name: enteredLandsAnnual
MK-CF-F-180.rule: Nothing unless EVERY earner typed a take-home above zero. Otherwise each earner's typed take-home — a monthly figure, whatever the pay frequency — × 12, added.

MK-CF-F-181.name: rateInForce
MK-CF-F-181.rule: In this order. (1) The person chose to type a rate: that percent ÷ 100, held between 0 and 1. (2) Yearly salary is above zero and every earner typed a take-home: rate = (yearly salary − 401(k) for the year − yearly take-home, never below 0) ÷ yearly salary, held between 0 and 1. Both of these count as the person's own. (3) Otherwise calculated: federal income tax plus state tax on the yearly taxed income (taxableAnnual) LESS the household's 401(k) contributions for the year — they come off before tax — ÷ the yearly taxed income, by filing status, with the standard deduction. 0 when there is no taxed income.

MK-CF-F-182.name: asPercent
MK-CF-F-182.rule: A rate × 100, to two decimals at most, followed by a percent sign.

MK-CF-F-183.name: paidOutByAccount
MK-CF-F-183.rule: Dividends, interest and coupons dated within the last year (on or after the same date last year), not reinvested, added by account.

MK-CF-F-184.name: incomeFromAccounts
MK-CF-F-184.rule: For each account, the first that applies. (1) It paid out more than zero over the last year (paidOutByAccount): that amount. (2) A bond: coupon rate × face value when both are above zero; else rate × balance when a rate is entered; else $0, marked as assumed. (3) Cash with a rate above zero: rate × balance. (4) Any other account with a balance above zero is named as not counted; foreign currency is skipped. Yearly income = the rows added.

MK-CF-F-185.name: needsTakeHomeConversion
MK-CF-F-185.rule: True when the pay was stored the old way — as take-home — and is above zero.

MK-CF-F-186.name: convertTakeHomeMode
MK-CF-F-186.rule: Unchanged unless it needs converting (needsTakeHomeConversion). Otherwise: yearly take-home = the stored figure × the periods in a year (weekly 52, every two weeks 26, monthly 12, hourly counted as 12); yearly gross = the gross whose federal tax leaves exactly that take-home (grossFromNet); the stored base pay becomes yearly gross ÷ periods; the typed take-home becomes the yearly take-home ÷ 12 — the month every screen now asks for; the mode becomes gross.

MK-CF-F-187.name: seniorDeductionFor
MK-CF-F-187.rule: 0 outside tax years 2025 to 2028; when filing separately; when nobody is 65 or over; or when the income is not known. Otherwise $6,000 × the people 65 or over (2 at most), less 6% of the income above $75,000 (single, head of household) or $150,000 (married); never below 0.

MK-CF-F-189.name: essentialsFromLoggedSpending
MK-CF-F-189.rule: Adds the logged expenses by calendar month. Looks at the 12 months BEFORE the current month. When at least one of those months holds any expense: average = their total ÷ the number of months that hold any — empty months are not counted as zero — labelled N month average. When none does: if the current month holds any, that month's total so far, labelled as one month; otherwise nothing.

MK-CF-F-190.name: essentialsMonthly
MK-CF-F-190.rule: The logged average (essentialsFromLoggedSpending) when there is one; otherwise the typed figure when it is above zero, labelled you entered; otherwise nothing.

MK-CF-F-191.name: ym
MK-CF-F-191.rule: A date written as year-month, for example 2026-08.

MK-CF-F-192.name: inflowLabel
MK-CF-F-192.rule: The prefix, then the source words in brackets joined by a plus sign — each word once, in the order given. With no sources: income (take-home).

MK-CF-F-193.name: inflowSourceWord
MK-CF-F-193.rule: The source lower-cased and trimmed. Starting with salary, base salary or paycheck → income (take-home). Starting with rental, or exactly rent → rent. Starting with social security → Social Security. Anything else → itself, with a trailing bracketed part removed.

MK-CF-F-194.name: monthOutflow
MK-CF-F-194.rule: With a stored record for the month: its expenses + its debt paid. With none: what has been logged so far.

MK-CF-F-195.name: monthsLeftInYear
MK-CF-F-195.rule: 12 − the number of months already finished this year: 12 in January, 1 in December. The current month counts as left.

MK-CF-F-196.name: perMonthToFill
MK-CF-F-196.rule: Room left ÷ the months left in the year (monthsLeftInYear), rounded to the nearest $100.

MK-CF-F-197.name: ageAttainedInYear
MK-CF-F-197.rule: This calendar year − the birth year. Nothing when the birth year is missing or before 1900.

MK-CF-F-198.name: payrollTaxWithheld
MK-CF-F-198.rule: On a year's wages (below zero counts as 0): 6.2% of the wages up to $184,500, plus 1.45% of all the wages, plus 0.9% of the wages above $200,000.

MK-CF-F-206.name: householdK401ByMonth
MK-CF-F-206.rule: For each earner: their monthly 401(k) in every month they have gross pay, and 0 in months they do not. Added over the earners, month by month.

MK-CF-F-210.name: annualOfSource
MK-CF-F-210.rule: A source stated per month: amount × 12. Per year: as it is. A salary row (stated as entered): the household's yearly salary (salaryAnnual), or the row's own amount when that is zero.

MK-CF-F-212.name: receivedInMonth
MK-CF-F-212.rule: The income records whose date begins with the year-month asked for, newest first.

MK-CF-O-001.name: basePay
MK-CF-O-001.rule: Runs earnerPay for each earner with the household's filing status (single when none), the number of people 65 or over, and the household's rate in force (rateInForce). Yearly gross = the earners' yearly gross added up. Take-home = their monthly take-homes added up. Tax band = the federal band on ALL the earners' wages together, by filing status; the band on the first earner's wage alone is also worked out, and when there are two or more earners, the two bands differ, and every earner typed a take-home, a note says so. When nobody typed a take-home the card states its own sum in words: gross in a month − tax − 401(k)s = take-home. Tax in a month = yearly gross × the rate in force ÷ 12. Mode: entered when every earner typed a take-home; calculated when none did; mixed otherwise. When the rate in force is the calculated one, short-by = Social Security and Medicare on each earner's yearly gross (payrollTaxWithheld), added up, ÷ 12; nothing otherwise. Every figure agrees only when every earner's check passes (payFiguresAgree). Monthly 401(k) = added up over the earners. Other taken in a month = each earner's everything-else added up; nothing when any earner's take-home is calculated.

MK-CF-O-002.name: expenses
MK-CF-O-002.rule: Recurring debt rows (recurringDebtPayments) and their total. Planned rows by category, as handed in, and their total. Actual expenses for the month — all, entered by hand, and imported (actualSpending). The debt payments that count as expenses (debtPaymentsCountedAsExpenses). Actual total = the actual expenses total + those debt payments. And the radar (radar).

MK-CF-O-003.name: thisMonth
MK-CF-O-003.rule: The planned block (plannedMonthFlow) and the actual block (actualMonthFlow), side by side.

MK-CF-O-004.name: incomeSummary
MK-CF-O-004.rule: TAKE-HOME rows — everything that arrives in a usual month; after tax means × (1 − the rate in force, rateInForce): each earner's take-home above zero (from basePay); tips after tax, only when every month has pay; self-employment after tax; rent after running costs — whole when the rate is the person's own, after tax when the app calculates it; interest and dividends paid to the bank, the same way — and when they are reinvested and the rate is calculated, a row of MINUS the tax on them; Social Security and pension after tax; other monthly income after tax, or whole when marked not taxable; benefits paid in all twelve months, support and monthly scholarships, whole. Usual month = the rows added up. Rent arriving in a month = the rent row's own amount, zero with no rental or a rental that loses money; it is handed out by name because the emergency fund counts it. Standout month = the largest of the twelve monthly take-home figures (incomeMonthlyGrid, take-home), shown only when it is more than $1 above the usual month; its note reads with the bonus when a bonus is entered and that is the bonus month (December when no month is set). TAXED rows, each only when above zero: each earner's yearly gross; rent, net, for the year; interest and dividends for the year; the bonus. Yearly taxed total = taxableAnnual. Band = the federal band on that total, by filing status. Tax = that total × the rate in force (rateInForce). Taxed but not received = interest and dividends in a month, unless they are paid to the bank. Ready when there is any salary or any taxed income. It also says how many earners have a wage entered, and marks each pay row as calculated or entered.

MK-CF-O-005.name: theContributionRoom
MK-CF-O-005.rule: Age = this calendar year − birth year; nothing with no birth year. 401(k): limit by age (annual401kLimit); used = monthly 401(k) × 12, never more than the limit; room = limit − used, never below 0. IRA: limit by age (annualIraLimit); used = monthly Roth IRA × 12, never more than the limit; room = limit − used. HSA: the self-only limit by age (annualHsaLimit), 0 when enrolled in Medicare; used = monthly HSA × 12, never more than the limit; room = limit − used. Catch-up flags: 401(k) and IRA at 50 or over; HSA at 55 or over. Months left = 12 − the months already finished this year (January 12, December 1). Per month to fill the 401(k) = room ÷ months left, to the nearest $100.

MK-CF-O-006.name: theCreditLine
MK-CF-O-006.rule: With no limit, or a limit of zero or less: no share used and no status. Otherwise share used = balance ÷ limit, rounded to three decimals; status good at 30% or under, caution above 30% up to 50%, high above 50%.

MK-CF-O-007.name: theTaxOrganizer
MK-CF-O-007.rule: Interest, dividends and coupons the accounts paid out over the last year (incomeFromAccounts), rounded to whole dollars, are handed with the profile, the accounts, the debts and the year (this year when none is given) to the tax organiser, whose answer is returned unchanged.

MK-CF-O-008.name: whatsComing
MK-CF-O-008.rule: The upcoming bills (upcomingBills) from the starting balance, today and the horizon given (365 days when none), soonest first; and the first of them as the next one — nothing when there are none.

MK-CF-O-010.name: theMonth
MK-CF-O-010.rule: The planned and actual blocks (thisMonth); the Expenses tab (expenses); committed = the monthly amounts of the goals added up; free = planned surplus − committed.

MK-CF-O-016.name: incomeSources
MK-CF-O-016.rule: One row for each of these, only when its amount is above zero: every earner with a base salary or a month table (steady or varies; named You or the spouse when there are two); self-employment (monthly or yearly, as entered); the bonus for the year, with its month; stock vesting for the year (rsuAnnual); rental property = net rent for the year ÷ 12, per month; Social Security and pension together, per month (retirementIncomeMonthly).

MK-CF-O-017.name: futurePaycheck
MK-CF-O-017.rule: Nothing when the age is unknown; when the person is at or past the retirement age (the plan's, else the profile's target, else 67); when the savings are zero or less; or when the projection gives nothing. Otherwise: the retirement projection is run to the retirement age and gives the projected savings at that age; the monthly draw those savings can support comes from buildPaycheckYear (solveSafeDraw); monthly paycheck = guaranteed income (Social Security, pension, annuity, other — guaranteedOutsideStreams) + that draw, each rounded to whole dollars.

MK-CF-O-018.name: theDebts
MK-CF-O-018.rule: Counts only debts with a balance above zero. Total = their balances added. Minimum in a month = each debt's minimum payment added, a debt due in full counting 0. Payments in a month = each debt's required payment added (requiredPayment). Interest in a month = balance × yearly rate ÷ 12, added over the debts. Plan in a month = the minimums + the extra. Progress: paid down = the debt at the start of the year − the total now; share = paid down ÷ the start-of-year debt; given only when the start-of-year debt and the paid-down amount are both above zero. The payoff plan is payoffPlan, with the extra and the method chosen (highest rate first when none is).

MK-NW-F-001.name: isAlternative
MK-NW-F-001.rule: True when the account's class (assetClassOf) is Alternatives.

MK-NW-F-002.name: alternativesSummary
MK-NW-F-002.rule: Over every account that holds alternatives, read from its class split (altPartsOf): count = how many such accounts; total = their alternatives parts added up, every part included — the same dollars as the Alternatives line; the parts no priced holding or option explains (asset type not classified) are added up on their own as the money not classified. Blended rate = each classified part × the yearly rate for its kind (the person's own rate for that kind first, else the benchmark), added up, ÷ the classified parts' total — no figure when that total is 0; growth in a year = the classified parts' total × blended rate, and no figure when it is 0 ($0 would read as a forecast). The rate and the growth leave the not-classified money out (DEC-4036h, 2026-10-10).

MK-NW-F-003.name: valueFreshness
MK-NW-F-003.rule: No answer for an account whose balance is built from its holdings, or one with no value date. Otherwise months old = the whole months that have fully passed since the value date: (years apart × 12 + calendar months apart), less 1 when today's day of the month is before the day the value was set — unless today is the last day of its month, which completes the month for a value set on a day that month does not have (a value set on the last day of January is one month old on the last day of February). A value dated by its month alone counts from the 1st, and its date is given as the 1st of that month. Never below zero. Stale when 6 or more.

MK-NW-F-004.name: portfolioActualReturn
MK-NW-F-004.rule: What the money set aside for retirement returned over the last twelve months — not the return of everything invested. Over accounts that are not property, that have a return for the last twelve months reported by the person (a reported 0 counts; one not reported is left out, never read as 0; a reported loss of everything or more is left out), and that have some amount set aside for retirement: each account's start = the amount set aside today ÷ (1 + its return). The answer = the amounts set aside today added up ÷ the starts added up − 1 — what the money set aside grew by, each account weighed by what was set aside when the twelve months began. No answer when either total is zero or less.

MK-NW-F-005.name: accountAllowsTicker
MK-NW-F-005.rule: False for property, for cash accounts, for a 529, and for checking and savings. Otherwise true when the account already lists holdings. Otherwise false for an account classed as Bonds & CDs or Alternatives (it is itself one bond, CD or alternative holding typed by hand), and true for everything else.

MK-NW-F-006.name: isCashKind
MK-NW-F-006.rule: True when the kind is a cash kind: checking, savings, high-yield savings, cash management or foreign currency. A money-market fund (Stocks / Funds) and a CD (Bonds & CDs) are not cash kinds — his rule DEC-0051.

MK-NW-F-007.name: assetKind
MK-NW-F-007.rule: Looks a kind up by its id in the app's list of account kinds and returns its entry (name, section, tax bucket, typical yearly return), or nothing when the id is not in the list. The id is matched exactly — capitals and spaces count — because only the app writes these ids; no id, or one typed another way, finds nothing.

MK-NW-F-008.name: incomeBearingClassOf
MK-NW-F-008.rule: From the account's name, capitals ignored, whole words only (put is not Putnam; cd is not ABCD), first match wins. Money market (also mmkt, mmf, or the ticker of a money-market fund) → Stocks / Funds — read before the sweep words, so a money-market settlement fund is the fund (the owner's rule of 2026-08-04). Then the words sweep or settlement → cash. The ticker of a Treasury-bill fund → Bonds & CDs. An option — an option code, a dated option, or the words put or call → Alternatives. Crypto — a coin's ticker, or the words bitcoin, ethereum or crypto → Alternatives. A commodity fund's ticker, or the words gold, silver, platinum, palladium or commodity unless the name is a company's → Alternatives. The words currency or forex, or the tickers FXE or FXY → Alternatives. The words CD, certificate of deposit, T-bill, Treasury bill, bond, note, treasury, muni, debenture or coupon — or a percent followed by the word due or a year → Bonds & CDs. Otherwise nothing: the name gives no evidence.

MK-NW-F-009.name: maturityClass
MK-NW-F-009.rule: Bonds & CDs when a maturity date is given that reads as a real calendar day — a full date (year-month-day), or a year and month alone, read as that month's first day; cash when none is. An empty or blank date counts as none, and so does a text that is not a real date (words such as 'tomorrow-ish', or a day that does not exist such as February 30) — owner rule DEC-4059b/c, 2026-10-10: dates are picked, never typed. It does not look at whether the date has passed.

MK-NW-F-010.name: wrapperAccount
MK-NW-F-010.rule: 401(k) → kind 401(k), pre-tax. Traditional IRA → kind Traditional IRA, pre-tax. Roth IRA → kind Roth IRA, Roth. Roth 401(k) → kind 401(k), Roth. HSA → kind HSA, pre-tax. Taxable → kind brokerage, taxable. Nothing chosen, or a word not on this list → no kind and no tax type: never assumed taxable (DEC-4036f, 2026-10-10).

MK-NW-F-011.name: assetClassOf
MK-NW-F-011.rule: The first of these that applies. (1) The class stated on the account. (2) Bonds & CDs if it has a maturity date (owner rule, 2026-08-04: any maturity-dated instrument is a bond) — whatever its name says. (3) The class its name is evidence for — except for a home, real estate, a vehicle or anything in the property bucket, whose name is a place and is not read. (4) The class of its kind: checking, savings, high-yield savings, cash management and foreign currency are cash; money market and stocks are Stocks / Funds; CD and fixed income are Bonds & CDs; private equity, hedge funds, commodities, crypto, annuities, options and other are Alternatives; home and real estate are Real estate; vehicle is Personal property. (5) Stocks / Funds if it lists holdings. (6) Cash if it is a cash account. (7) If it is property: Real estate when no kind is recorded or its use (lived in, rented, second home, land) is recorded; Personal property for any other kind. (8) Otherwise Unclassified.

MK-NW-F-012.name: taxTreatmentOf
MK-NW-F-012.rule: A 529 is tax-free whatever is stored (what it earns comes out untaxed when used for education; DEC-4036d, 2026-10-10). An HSA is tax-deferred — pre-tax going in — whatever bucket it is filed in (DEC-4036e, 2026-10-10). Otherwise the tax treatment stated on the account. Otherwise by its tax bucket — the one on the account when it is one of cash, pre-tax, Roth, taxable or property, else the bucket its kind carries when that bucket is not taxable — a kind whose catalogue bucket is taxable (crypto, a bond, a CD, a brokerage) says nothing about tax (DEC-4036f, 2026-10-10): no bucket at all → tax type not stated, never assumed taxable (DEC-4036f, 2026-10-10); pre-tax → tax-deferred; Roth → tax-free; anything else → taxable.

MK-NW-F-013.name: realEstateUseOf
MK-NW-F-013.rule: An account that is not real estate has no use (no answer). Land stated as land is land. Asked about one property with neither the household nor the rent entries: its stated use, else the home. Given the household or the rent entries: what propertyUseMap says of it — home is the home lived in, rental is a rental (only when a rent entry handed in names it), anything else is a second home.

MK-NW-F-014.name: isRealAsset
MK-NW-F-014.rule: True when the account's class (assetClassOf) is Real estate or Personal property.

MK-NW-F-015.name: totalAssets
MK-NW-F-015.rule: Every account's balance added up; a missing balance counts as zero.

MK-NW-F-016.name: cashTotal
MK-NW-F-016.rule: For an account that has a class split (accountClassBreakdown): the cash part of it — a linked account's uninvested cash, or the uninvested cash an account built by hand records for itself. For any other account: its whole balance when its class is cash, otherwise nothing. Added up over every account.

MK-NW-F-017.name: equitiesTotal
MK-NW-F-017.rule: The Stocks / Funds line of the class split (assetAllocation): everything classed as Stocks / Funds, wherever it sits. An account holding several classes gives only its Stocks / Funds part.

MK-NW-F-018.name: fixedIncomeTotal
MK-NW-F-018.rule: The Bonds & CDs line of the class split (assetAllocation): everything classed as Bonds & CDs, wherever it sits. An account holding several classes gives only its Bonds & CDs part.

MK-NW-F-019.name: alternativesTotal
MK-NW-F-019.rule: The Alternatives line of the class split (assetAllocation): everything classed as Alternatives, wherever it sits. An account holding several classes gives only its Alternatives part.

MK-NW-F-020.name: realEstateTotal
MK-NW-F-020.rule: The Real estate line of the class split (assetAllocation): everything classed as Real estate.

MK-NW-F-021.name: investmentsTotal
MK-NW-F-021.rule: The Investments line on Net worth: the Stocks / Funds, Bonds & CDs, Alternatives and Unclassified lines of the class split (assetAllocation), added up. Cash sitting uninvested inside an investment account is on the Cash line (cashTotal), not here; a CD inside a cash account is here. Always: cashTotal + investmentsTotal = investableAssets.

MK-NW-F-022.name: investableAssets
MK-NW-F-022.rule: The balances of every account that is not a real asset (isRealAsset), added up by sumWhere — an account with no balance is left out, not counted as zero.

MK-NW-F-023.name: wrapperWord
MK-NW-F-023.rule: The word for a kind: checking → Checking; savings → Savings; high-yield savings; money market; CD; cash management; foreign currency → Foreign currency; brokerage, stocks, fixed income, commodities and options → Brokerage; annuities → Annuity; 401(k); Traditional IRA; Roth IRA; HSA; 529; Home; Vehicle. Crypto, private equity, hedge funds and other name what is held, not an account: nothing, unless the person confirmed the account is a brokerage. Nothing for an unknown kind or none.

MK-NW-F-024.name: accountLastFour
MK-NW-F-024.rule: From the account's mask, or failing that its account number: drop everything but digits; if four or more digits remain, the last four; otherwise nothing.

MK-NW-F-025.name: accountDisplayName
MK-NW-F-025.rule: The kind word is wrapperWord for the account (401(k), Traditional IRA, Roth IRA, HSA, 529, Brokerage, Checking and so on; none for a kind that names contents, such as crypto, unless confirmed a brokerage). An account is tax-advantaged only when taxTreatmentOf says tax-deferred or tax-free — a tax type not stated is not (DEC-4036f, 2026-10-10). For a tax-advantaged account: where the kind says only Brokerage — or there is no kind and the last four digits are known — the word is Roth when the account is tax-free and 401(k) / IRA when it is tax-deferred; a 401(k) in the Roth bucket or tax-free is Roth 401(k). A tax-advantaged account always shows what it is. With an institution: a tax-advantaged account that has a word reads Institution + word + -last four (without the digits when unknown); otherwise with digits it reads Institution -last four; otherwise Institution + kind word. With none of those: the account's own name (an account named Imported holding with exactly one holding takes that holding's ticker or name), with the institution in front only if the name does not already contain it, and the mask at the end only if it is not already there.

MK-NW-F-026.name: accountDisplayNames
MK-NW-F-026.rule: Each account gets its display name (accountDisplayName). Where two or more accounts end up with the same name, each gets · 1, · 2 and so on added, in the order of their account ids read as text (an id is made by the app from the moment the account was created, so that is the order they were made). A numbered name that is already another account's name is skipped, so no two accounts are ever shown by the same name.

MK-NW-F-027.name: accountClassBreakdown
MK-NW-F-027.rule: LINKED ACCOUNT. Cash = its cash balance. Each holding with a price = shares × last price, filed under its class (holdingClassOf). Each option = its value as synced, under Alternatives (an option is valued when it is synced, at contracts × price per share × 100 — owner, 2026-08-26). If the parts come to less than the balance and one or more holdings have NO price: the whole difference is filed under the unpriced holdings' class when they share one, and under Unclassified when they span classes — never under cash. Otherwise, if the parts do not add up to the balance: a difference no bigger than the larger of $1 or 1% of the balance is added to cash when positive (owner rule, 2026-08-11), or taken off the largest class when negative; a bigger one is put under the account's own class (assetClassOf). ACCOUNT BUILT BY HAND (not a cash or property account): when it records its own cash (or its balance is built from its records) and its balance is below zero, the whole balance is cash — overdrawn is negative cash: balance −$100 with a cash field of $50 is Cash −$100 (DEC-4036i, 2026-10-10). Otherwise its cash = the uninvested cash it records, above zero, never more than the balance, when its balance is built from its records or it records cash. When its balance is built from its holdings, each holding is weighed at today's value — shares × the broker's price, else the value its balance was last built from, else what was paid — and the rest of the balance is shared out among the holdings' classes by those weights, so a T-bill is Bonds & CDs; if every holding is of the account's own class, the rest stays whole under that class. No answer when it records no cash and its holdings are all of its own class. ANY OTHER ACCOUNT — a typed balance, a bank account — gets no answer. The parts always add up to the balance.

MK-NW-F-028.name: classPortionLabel
MK-NW-F-028.rule: The words for one class inside one account, counting the holdings of that class (holdingClassOf — the same test the dollars beside the words were split by). Cash: cash in this account. Bonds: counts the holdings whose name has the whole word CD (or certificate of deposit), those whose name has the whole word Treasury (or Treas, UST, T-bill, T-note, T-bond, government — the broker's wording too), capitals ignored, and the rest as bonds; a count of one is singular, any other count takes its plural from the one list of words (plural, the one list of words — his ruling of 2026-10-10 — Treasuries for more than one), a count of zero is left out, two parts are joined with &, three as A, B & C — for example 3 CDs & 1 Treasury in this account, or 1 CD, 1 Treasury & 2 bonds in this account — or bonds & CDs in this account when none are listed. Stocks: N holdings in this account (1 holding), or stocks & funds in this account when none are listed. Alternatives: N options & N holdings in this account, each part left out when its count is zero (an option is one option position, however many contracts), or alternatives in this account. Any other class: unpriced portion of this account.

MK-NW-F-029.name: assetAllocation
MK-NW-F-029.rule: The value in each asset class across every account. An account with a class split (accountClassBreakdown) — a linked account, or an account built by hand that records its own uninvested cash — is split by it; any other account counts whole under its one class (assetClassOf). The seven classes add to everything owned, and the Cash class is cashTotal.

MK-NW-F-030.name: earmarkDefault
MK-NW-F-030.rule: The share of an account counted towards retirement by default (owner, 2026-08-11, DEC-0100: all assets minus the home lived in and the car driven): 0% for a 529, for the car driven (primaryCarIdOf), and for the home lived in. Told the household's home (its identifier, from primaryHomeIdOf), only that property is 0%; told the household has no home (null), no property is; told nothing, a property stated as the home lived in, or with no use stated, is 0%. 100% for everything else — a rental, a second home, a second car, valuables included.

MK-NW-F-031.name: primaryCarIdOf
MK-NW-F-031.rule: Among the accounts whose kind is vehicle, and no other: the vehicles whose value is entered are the candidates — a vehicle with no value is not ranked as $0 (DEC-4036j, 2026-10-10); when none has a value, every vehicle is. Of the candidates, the one with the largest balance; a tie goes to the lower id read as text (the one made first). Nothing when there is no vehicle. Valuables and other personal property are never the car.

MK-NW-F-032.name: earmarkedAmount
MK-NW-F-032.rule: Balance × the share earmarked for retirement. The share is the one stated on the account, held between 0% and 100%, or the default (earmarkDefault, told which car is driven and which property is lived in, or that there is none) when none is stated.

MK-NW-F-033.name: retirementEarmarkedValue
MK-NW-F-033.rule: Every account's earmarked amount (earmarkedAmount) added up, with the car driven found by primaryCarIdOf and the home lived in by primaryHomeIdOf.

MK-NW-F-034.name: benchmarkReturn
MK-NW-F-034.rule: The person's own yearly rate for that kind where they set one — a rate of exactly 0 counts as set. Otherwise the app's typical yearly return for the kind: checking 0.5%, savings 2.4%, high-yield savings 4.2%, money market 4.5%, CD 4.2%, cash management 3.5%, foreign currency 0%, brokerage 8%, stocks and funds 10.4%, fixed income 4.2%, crypto 8%, private equity 13%, hedge funds 6%, gold and commodities 8.2%, options 5%, annuities 4.5%, 529 7%, other 5%, 401(k), IRA, Roth IRA and HSA 7.9%, home 4.5%, vehicle −5%. 6% for a kind that is unknown or missing. A kind is matched exactly as the app writes it; capitals count.

MK-NW-F-035.name: blendedVolatility
MK-NW-F-035.rule: Over exactly the accounts the nest egg counts: each account's volatility — the person's own figure for its kind, else the app's figure for the kind, else 12% — averaged, weighted by its earmarked amount. No answer when nothing is earmarked (the Plan then uses the band its growth rate implies, chosen at its call site). It is a weighted average of the parts, which is the portfolio's own volatility only when the parts move together; a table of how the classes move together is not yet built.

MK-NW-F-036.name: benchmarkInfo
MK-NW-F-036.rule: The rate from benchmarkReturn, with where it came from. Edited = the person set a rate for that kind (0 included): then the source reads Your custom estimate, the period is blank and estimate is true (a person's own rate is an assumption). Otherwise the source and period on record for that kind, and estimate = whether that record is marked an assumption rather than a measured index; a kind with no record reads Generic blended estimate, period blank, estimate true.

MK-NW-F-037.name: blendedReturn
MK-NW-F-037.rule: Over exactly the accounts the nest egg counts (every account, each weighted by its earmarked amount — the home lived in, the car driven and a 529 weigh nothing by default, a rental weighs its full value): the benchmark yearly rate of each account's kind (benchmarkReturn), averaged, weighted by its earmarked amount. No answer when the earmarked total is zero — the Plan then chooses its own 6% at its call site, and says so there.

MK-NW-F-038.name: earmarkedKinds
MK-NW-F-038.rule: The distinct kinds among accounts that are not property and have an earmarked amount above zero. An account with no kind counts as other.

MK-NW-F-039.name: buildAssetsState
MK-NW-F-039.rule: A balance that is missing (blank, or not a number) is left out. Total = the balances that are there, added up. Each account's share = its balance ÷ total × 100, or 0 when the total is 0 or its balance is missing (an overdrawn account has a negative share; the shares still add to 100). Average target return = each account's target return weighted by its balance; no answer when the total is 0.

MK-NW-F-040.name: assetsFromOnboarding
MK-NW-F-040.rule: Makes up to four accounts from the setup answers, skipping an answer left blank or below zero (a typed 0 is kept): traditional retirement savings → a pre-tax 401(k); Roth retirement savings → a Roth IRA; investment holdings → taxable stocks and funds; each of those three gets a target return of 7%. Savings or portfolio → an Unclassified account with no kind, no tax type and a target return of 0, marked to be asked: Is this cash savings or investments? (DEC-4036g, 2026-10-10).

MK-NW-F-041.name: monthlyContributionsFromOnboarding
MK-NW-F-041.rule: No answer when none of the contribution questions was answered (401(k), Roth, investing, employer match). Otherwise, a month's retirement contributions = the 401(k) amount, held at the year's elective limit for the person's age ÷ 12 (2026: $24,500 under 50, $32,500 at 50 to 59 and 64 and over, $35,750 at 60 to 63), + the Roth amount as entered (the question does not say Roth IRA or Roth 401(k), whose limits differ, so it is not held at either), + the investing amount, + the employer's match for a month (the stated share of the 401(k) amount AFTER it is held at the limit — an employer matches only what can go in — or the stated dollars). Money saved toward a property (an older setup question) is not a retirement contribution and is left out. The age is the one attained this year, from the birth year.
