MK-NW-F-044.name: getAssetsState
MK-NW-F-044.rule: Reads the saved accounts and returns assetsStateFrom of them: nothing when none are saved or the saved list is empty.

MK-NW-F-045.name: sourceWording
MK-NW-F-045.rule: Linked account: Linked — or Linked · N days old when its last successful update is 4 or more days old, and Linked · not updated yet when no update is on record (no age is invented). Imported account: Imported, by the same test. Anything else: By hand · you update it. The timestamp read is the account's last successful sync.

MK-NW-F-046.name: historyCoverage
MK-NW-F-046.rule: Entered by hand: a sentence saying it has no activity records. The history start is the person's own date when they entered one (DEC-4059c, 2026-10-10 — it outranks the date the sync read), otherwise the date the sync recorded. Linked with no history start on record: a sentence saying none has been shared yet. A history start that is not a real calendar date, or is after today: the refusal 'History start date cannot be read.' with no months figure and no start date — the screen offers 'Edit date' (owner rule DEC-4059c, 2026-10-10). History starting on or before the period's first day: nothing to say. Otherwise: months covered = the whole months from the history start to today plus the part month (days ÷ the days in that month), rounded DOWN to one decimal; the sentence is built from the whole months only and names the start date: N years when the whole months are an exact multiple of twelve and there is no part month, N years and a bit when there is, N years M months when twelve or more, N months when one or more, otherwise a few days. Year and month take their plural from the one list of words (plural, the one list of words — his ruling of 2026-10-10): 1 year, 1 month. It never rounds up.

MK-NW-F-047.name: uberGroupOf
MK-NW-F-047.rule: Cash → Cash. Stocks / Funds, Bonds & CDs, Alternatives and Unclassified → Investments. Real estate and Personal property → Personal property.

MK-NW-F-048.name: uberGroupRows
MK-NW-F-048.rule: Sorts the class rows into the three groups, in the order Cash, Investments, Personal property: Cash ← cash; Investments ← Stocks / Funds, Bonds & CDs, Alternatives, Unclassified; Personal property (the third group, which the screen labels so) ← Real estate, Personal property. A group's total = its classes' totals added up, in the order the rows came; the groups add to What you own. A group with no classes is left out.

MK-NW-F-049.name: itemizedTotal
MK-NW-F-049.rule: The values of the listed holdings that have one, added up in exact decimals; a holding with no value is left out (itemizeMissingCount counts it), never counted as zero; a negative value counts.

MK-NW-F-050.name: itemizeRemainder
MK-NW-F-050.rule: The entered balance less itemizedTotal, in exact decimals (an entered total that equals its holdings leaves exactly 0, never a stray fraction of a cent). Positive: some is still unexplained. Negative: the holdings add up to more than was entered.

MK-NW-F-051.name: itemizedResultTotal
MK-NW-F-051.rule: The account's total after itemising: the holdings added up, plus what is still unallocated when that is above zero (it stays as cash) — so it is the entered total until the holdings listed come to more than the entered total, when it is their sum. The screen shows the new total before the person taps Done.

MK-NW-F-052.name: buildItemizedAccounts
MK-NW-F-052.rule: Refused when any listed holding has no value (the refusal counts them with plural, the one list of words — his ruling of 2026-10-10) — nothing is built, so the account stays as it was. Otherwise one account for each listed holding: named by its label, else its ticker, else Holding; with the original's institution and tax bucket, and what the original carried — its retirement share, its source, and its wrapper kind when the original is a 401(k), IRA, Roth IRA, HSA or 529 (otherwise the kind for the class); balance = its value; class as given; its yearly rate = the benchmark for its class's kind (benchmarkReturn), never 0. A bond also carries its maturity date, its rate only when one was entered, and its face value only when the person entered one — never today's value in its place. What is still unallocated, when above zero, becomes one more account named institution + cash, with the same share, source and wrapper, at the cash-management benchmark rate.

MK-NW-F-053.name: correctClassOf
MK-NW-F-053.rule: The class an account SHOULD have, or nothing when there is no correction to make. A class the person chose is the class it should carry. Otherwise, in the order assetClassOf reads: Bonds & CDs if it has a maturity date; else the class its name is evidence for — never for a home, real estate, a vehicle or anything in the property bucket, whose name is a place; else Stocks / Funds for a money market account; else Bonds & CDs for a CD.

MK-NW-F-054.name: reclassifyAccounts
MK-NW-F-054.rule: For each account the person has NOT confirmed (an account they confirmed is left exactly as it is): if the person did not choose its class and correctClassOf gives a class different from the one it carries, it takes that class (a cash tax bucket becomes no tax type stated unless the new class is cash — never taxable, DEC-4036f, 2026-10-10). For each holding inside it: a holding the person classed, or one waiting on their answer, is left as it is; otherwise, when its ticker and name are evidence for a class other than cash and its stored tag means another class, it is stored under that class — bond for Bonds & CDs, other for Alternatives (Gold), stock_etf for Stocks / Funds. No evidence leaves it as it is. Returns the accounts and how many changes were made.

MK-NW-F-055.name: isBond
MK-NW-F-055.rule: True when the account's class (assetClassOf) is Bonds & CDs.

MK-NW-F-056.name: bondInfo
MK-NW-F-056.rule: Reads a bond's facts off its account: face value (not entered when missing or zero or less), yearly rate (not entered when missing; a typed zero is kept), maturity date, value (the balance), accrued interest (not entered when missing), whether it is a CD — its kind is a CD, or its own name says CD or certificate of deposit; its institution is never read for this (DEC-4036c, 2026-10-10) — and where a CD was bought: through a broker only when the person said so, otherwise from the bank (DEC-3837, 2026-10-10).

MK-NW-F-057.name: annualCoupon
MK-NW-F-057.rule: Face value × yearly interest rate. Nothing when either was not entered.

MK-NW-F-058.name: yearsToMaturity
MK-NW-F-058.rule: Exact years to maturity, by anniversaries: the whole years counted back from the maturity date while still on or after today, plus the days from today to the first of those anniversaries ÷ the days in that year. One year to the day is exactly 1. Zero when the date is today or past. By the calendar date, never the time of day. Nothing when there is no date or the day does not exist (a day past the end of its month is not rolled into the next month).

MK-NW-F-059.name: currentYield
MK-NW-F-059.rule: yearlyInterest ÷ the value as entered (the statement's market value, which leaves accrued interest out — his ruling of 2026-10-09). Nothing when no rate was entered, or when the value is zero or less.

MK-NW-F-060.name: approxYTM
MK-NW-F-060.rule: Nothing when there is no maturity date or the bond has matured. A CD bought from the bank (pricedLikeBond says no): its stated rate, even when no face value was entered, and nothing when no rate was entered (DEC-3837, 2026-10-10). A bond, or a CD bought through a broker: nothing when no face value or no rate was entered, or when its value is zero or less; else the yield y at which priceAtYield equals the full price — the value as entered plus accrued interest (as entered, else estimatedAccrued; his ruling of 2026-10-09) — found by halving the interval two hundred times.

MK-NW-F-061.name: bondSummary
MK-NW-F-061.rule: Count = how many bonds. Total value = each value added up. Total face value = each face value added up, a face not entered counting as zero (the bonds without one are named apart by theBonds). Interest in a year = yearlyInterestNow of each, added up: a bond past its maturity date counts $0, and a bond with no rate counts as zero. Average yield is over the bonds that have a value today AND a rate AND are not past their maturity date: their yearlyInterest ÷ their value today as entered; nothing when no bond qualifies. Next maturity = the earliest maturity date AFTER today, by the calendar — a bond maturing today has matured and is not next.

MK-NW-F-062.name: couponIncomeAnnual
MK-NW-F-062.rule: Over the accounts that are bonds or CDs: yearlyInterestNow of each, added up — $0 for one past its maturity date, and one with no rate counting as zero.

MK-NW-F-063.name: interestIncomeAnnual
MK-NW-F-063.rule: For a bond or CD: nothing when it is past its maturity date (isPastMaturity, by the calendar; no date or an impossible one is not past); otherwise yearlyInterest (face × rate; with no face, balance × rate; with no rate, nothing). For a cash account that states a rate: balance × rate. Nothing for anything else. Added up over every account.

MK-NW-F-064.name: bondRateSensitivity
MK-NW-F-064.rule: Nothing for a CD bought from the bank (pricedLikeBond says no; a CD bought through a broker is priced like a bond, DEC-3837, 2026-10-10), when the yield to maturity is unknown, when the bond cannot be priced (matured or no date), or when the face value or rate was not entered or is zero or less. For rates one percentage point UP and one DOWN: the change = priceAtYield at the yield to maturity plus or minus one point (never below 0.01%) less priceAtYield at the yield to maturity itself. The new price = today's value + that change. It gives a range from 1% under to 1% over the new price, and the change, each rounded in proportion to the bond: to the nearest $1,000 for a bond worth $100,000 or more, the nearest $100 from $10,000, the nearest $10 from $1,000, and so on down.

MK-NW-F-065.name: buildNetWorth
MK-NW-F-065.rule: Net worth = total assets − total debt, returned with both totals.

MK-NW-F-066.name: sumWhere
MK-NW-F-066.rule: Over the accounts that pass the given test: the total = the balances that exist, added up (a negative balance counts), and beside it how many have no balance. A missing balance is never counted as zero. Nothing passing the test is a total of 0 with nothing missing.

MK-NW-F-067.name: plural
MK-NW-F-067.rule: The count followed by the noun: the noun for exactly 1, otherwise its plural from the one list of words the app counts in words, PLURAL_WORDS (his ruling, 2026-10-10) — Treasury → Treasuries, property → properties, every other word on it adds s; zero takes the plural. The count is written as the caller gives it (a formatted figure or a number word) when one is given, otherwise the number. A word not on the list is refused (an error) in tests and development, never given a guessed s; a release build writes the word unchanged.

MK-NW-F-068.name: prettyDay
MK-NW-F-068.rule: Reads a date written year-month-day as a calendar date — never through a clock or a time zone — and writes the short month name (Jan … Dec, Sep not Sept), the day without a leading zero, a comma and the year. An empty or impossible date gives nothing.

MK-NW-F-069.name: priceAtYield
MK-NW-F-069.rule: Nothing when the bond has matured or has no maturity date, when no face value above zero was entered, or when 1 + yield is zero or less. Otherwise t = yearsToMaturity, exact; the yearly coupon (face × rate; zero when no rate was entered) falls on each maturity anniversary, at t, t − 1, … down to the last above zero; price = each coupon ÷ (1 + yield) to the power of its time, added up, plus face ÷ (1 + yield) to the power t.

MK-NW-F-070.name: accruedInterestCaveat
MK-NW-F-070.rule: When accrued interest was not entered and estimatedAccrued gives an estimate (a bond or a CD bought through a broker that pays interest, not a CD bought from the bank, not matured, not on a coupon day): his words — Added estimated $<the estimate, whole dollars> in accrued interest to bond value at <the rate>% coupon for <days> days (1 day for one; the plural from plural, the one list of words — his ruling of 2026-10-10) to calculate YTM. If this is not accurate, enter actual accrued interest. Otherwise nothing.

MK-NW-F-071.name: isCertificateOfDeposit
MK-NW-F-071.rule: True when bondInfo says the account is a CD: its kind is a CD, or its own name contains the whole word CD, or the words certificate of deposit, in any capitals. The institution's name is never read: a brokerage account at CD Capital is not a CD (DEC-4036c, 2026-10-10).

MK-NW-F-072.name: rowOf
MK-NW-F-072.rule: One row for one bond: face value and yearly interest rate (each not entered when it was not), interest paid in a year (yearlyInterestNow: face × rate; with no face, value × rate; with no rate, not entered; $0 once past its maturity date, so the rows add up to the summary), maturity date, years left (yearsToMaturity — exact, never below zero), current yield, yield to maturity (approxYTM — solved exactly; nothing when matured), value, whether it is a CD, whether it is priced like a bond (pricedLikeBond: a bond, or a CD bought through a broker), and the accrued-interest note (accruedInterestCaveat, worked for today). The heading is the institution when it is not blank after trimming, otherwise the account's name.

MK-NW-F-073.name: itemising
MK-NW-F-073.rule: Returns four things. Keep-total-at = the balance the account was entered at. Itemised = the values of the listed holdings that have one, added up. Remainder = the entered balance less that sum. Remainder-final = false when any listed holding has no value (the remainder is then not final, never called unexplained).

MK-NW-F-084.name: categoryEarnings
MK-NW-F-084.rule: Uses the dividend and interest records dated on or after the period's first day, amounts taken as positive. A record that names a ticker goes to that holding's category: bond → Bonds & CDs; cash → Cash in this account; anything else → Stocks / Funds; a ticker with no holding on record → Stocks / Funds for a dividend, Bonds & CDs for interest. A record that names NO ticker → Stocks / Funds for a dividend; for interest, Bonds & CDs when the record's account is a bond or CD account handed in, else Cash in this account. A category's return, over the holdings with a value above zero and a period return above −100%: each holding's value at the start = its value now ÷ (1 + its return over the whole period, never a yearly rate); return = the values now added up ÷ the values at the start added up − 1. Nothing when no holding qualifies. Bonds & CDs shows a stated YEARLY rate instead — each bond account's rate weighted by its balance — when every bond account with a balance states a rate and no bond is held as a holding. On day one all three categories are returned with no return; any other day only the categories that earned more than zero.

MK-NW-F-090.name: windowStartKey
MK-NW-F-090.rule: Since: the day after the earliest recorded day, but never later than today; today when nothing is recorded. This year: 1 January of today's year. 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y and 2Y: today moved back 1, 3, 6, 12 or 24 months — the same day of that month, or its last day when that month is shorter (one month before 31 March is 28 February). Any other label: 12 months back, the same way.

MK-NW-F-091.name: pricedGainOf
MK-NW-F-091.rule: Each holding's gain over the period, added up. For a holding bought inside the period: its whole gain (value − cost). For any other holding with a period return: value × (1 − 1 ÷ (1 + return)) when its value is above zero, which is today's value less its value when the period opened; nothing when it holds nothing. For a holding with no period return that states a yearly rate (only a certificate of deposit is given one): value × (1 − 1 ÷ (1 + rate) to the power years), years handed in (none handed in counts as 0, so it gains nothing). Any other holding that holds something (its value, or the broker's last price × its shares, or the value it was entered at, above zero) has a gain that cannot be known: the answer is then NOTHING — not zero — for the whole total. A holding that holds nothing gains nothing. (Owner decision DEC-3656, 2026-10-09.)

MK-NW-F-092.name: investmentAccountIdsOf
MK-NW-F-092.rule: The ids of the accounts whose class is Stocks / Funds, Bonds & CDs, Alternatives or Unclassified. Cash and property accounts are left out.

MK-NW-F-094.name: ledgerGroups
MK-NW-F-094.rule: Groups the accounts for the Net worth list, by asset-class label or by institution. By class: an account with a class split (accountClassBreakdown) is a row under EVERY class it has a part in, at that part; any other account is one row, whole, under its one class. Each group's total = its rows added up (his ruling, 2026-10-07: the rows under a heading add up to the heading). By institution (an account with no institution goes under No institution set; names are matched trimmed, capitals ignored, and the group shows the first spelling seen): each account is one row at its balance, a group's total = those balances added up, and the group lists the classes inside it with their totals, from the same split, largest first. Group totals by class equal the class rows; both views add to everything owned.

MK-NW-F-103.name: investmentRecordDates
MK-NW-F-103.rule: The dates of the recorded days that hold a value for at least one of the named accounts, oldest first. Empty when no accounts are named.

MK-NW-O-001.name: theBonds
MK-NW-O-001.rule: Takes every account that is a bond or CD. Rows are sorted by maturity date, soonest first, with any that has no date last. Count, total value, total face value, interest in a year, average yield and next maturity come from bondSummary. When one bond is opened it also gives: matured = its maturity date is today or earlier, by the calendar (a bond with no date has not matured — it is unknown); a matured bond gives no yield to maturity and no rate-move figure; and what a move in interest rates would do to its value (bondRateSensitivity) — except for a CD bought from the bank, where no figure is given and a sentence says a CD is not traded and is worth its balance until it matures; a CD bought through a broker gets the figure like a bond and no sentence (DEC-3837, 2026-10-10). It also names the bonds the average yield leaves out — those with no value today, and, apart, those with a value but no rate entered — and the bonds with no face value entered, so a screen can say which.

figures_checked_by_hand.3837: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-3837 (2026-10-10) that this rule follows

MK-NW-O-002.name: theAccount
MK-NW-O-002.rule: Uses the records whose account is this account, and any transfer that arrives in it from another account. Market value = the account's balance. Income = dividends + interest in those records, to the cent — and NO FIGURE when the account has no records at all. Inside = for a linked account, the value in each asset class that is not zero (accountClassBreakdown); for any other account, nothing. Activity = every record with its date, type, ticker and amount: the amount is the record's effect on cash, except a transfer INTO this account, which shows the amount moved; a record counts as the person's own unless it came through the link. Income of one holding = dividends and interest whose record names that holding's ticker, capitals ignored; a record naming no ticker belongs to no holding.

MK-NW-O-003.name: theNetWorth
MK-NW-O-003.rule: Assets = every account's balance added up. Debts = every debt's remaining balance added up. Net worth = assets − debts. Cash = cashTotal. Investments = investmentsTotal: the investment classes of the class split added up (Stocks / Funds, Bonds & CDs, Alternatives, Unclassified, from assetAllocation) — so a linked account's uninvested cash is in Cash only, and Cash + Investments + property comes to everything owned. Investable = investableAssets. By class = assetAllocation. Each debt is listed with its balance and its required monthly payment (the larger of its minimum and the payment the person says they make); monthly debt payments = those added up; monthly debt minimum = the minimums alone added up. Return on cash + investments = a TIME-WEIGHTED return (owner decision, 2026-10-04: "All return should be True Weighted Return and not Dietz return.") over every account that is not property: the period from the day compared from to today is split at every day money moved in or out; each piece = the value just before the next movement ÷ the value just after the last one; the pieces are multiplied and 1 is taken off; returned as a share. A month given without a day is read as its first day. Cash earns only interest: any other change in a cash account's balance is money moving, counted on the day the record first shows it. For the other accounts, money moving = deposits, withdrawals and cash transferred between accounts. Today's value is read from the accounts as they stand. No figure when no day is given, when no recorded day on or before the day compared from holds the accounts, when money moved on a day with no recorded value, when a deposit, withdrawal or transfer on a measured account has no amount on record, or when shares were moved in or out. It also hands out the match of mortgages to properties (mortgagesByProperty). It also names the holdings nothing could class and the person has not yet answered about (account, holding), and the sentence that asks.

MK-NW-O-004.name: theEmergencyFund
MK-NW-O-004.rule: Cash = all cash (cashTotal), or the amount handed in when one is given. Owner rule, 2026-10-04: "Once user enters mortgage or any debt - the app deduct it directly to calculate surplus, emergency fund, and any other place instead of leaving it for user to add it to planned expenses." Debt minimums = the MINIMUM monthly payment of every debt added up — the home's mortgage included; a balance due in one lump has none. A payment a person chooses to make above the minimum is not counted: it can be stopped. The budget is read as it is counted (theBudgetCounted): where the home's mortgage is in Debts, the Rent / Mortgage budget line is counted as nothing, and the screen is given a sentence saying so. Essentials for a month = essential expenses + debt minimums. Essential expenses = the average of what was logged, over the calendar months of the last twelve that have a logged entry (this month alone when only it has one); the typed plan only when nothing is logged. Left out of that average, so nothing is counted twice: a payment logged against a debt that is entered (an expense in the category Debt payment, named for that debt), and, where the home's mortgage is in Debts, anything logged under Rent / Mortgage. Rent that keeps arriving = the Rent row of the Income summary (rent from a property less what it costs to run, less calculated tax when the tax rate is calculated), never below zero; owner, 2026-10-04: "add it to the cash as losing job does not mean loosing rental income too." It arrives every month, so it is added to the cash every month. From cash each month = essentials − that rent, never below zero. Months covered = cash ÷ from cash each month; no figure when essentials are zero, and no figure when the rent pays for the whole month (the cash is then not drawn on, and it says so). Planned = planned monthly expenses + debt minimums; months covered at the planned level = cash ÷ (planned − that rent); no figure when that is zero or less. Target for N months = from cash each month × N; gap = target − cash, never below zero. Months left after a shock = (cash − the shock, never below zero) ÷ from cash each month. When a typed month of essentials is handed in, it stands in for essentials + debt minimums. A target, and the months left after a shock, are given only when there is an essentials figure. Rent not known, owner rule 2026-10-10 (instead of showing nothing, the card says the months are counted with the rent not included, and asks for the rent): the answer also says whether a property's rent is not known. It is not known only when the household holds a property that is not the home (home, rental and second home read by the owner's property-use rule of 2026-10-04) AND one of these holds: a rent entry's rent figure is blank or not a plain number, or the entry names no property (it is not counted as rent, owner rule DEC-4059d, 2026-10-10); with no list of rent entries, the single typed rent figure is typed at all (it names no property, so it is not counted, DEC-4059d); the rent entries are stored in a shape that is not a list; or with no rent entries stored at all, a property is kept as a rental. A property with no rent entry when rent entries are stored is a second home, not a missing rent. A household with no property other than the home is never flagged. The months covered are still given, counted without the unknown rent.

MK-NW-O-005.name: theAlternativesOutlook
MK-NW-O-005.rule: Count, total value and blended rate come from alternativesSummary: over every account that holds alternatives, its alternatives part (altPartsOf) — the same dollars the Net worth tab's Alternatives line counts. Blended rate: over the classified parts only; no figure when nothing classified is held. Growth in a year = alternativesSummary's growth (the classified parts × blended rate), given only when there is at least one such account and the total is above zero; otherwise no figure. Money not classified = the parts no priced holding or option explains; when it is not 0 the summary says: Expected return and growth leave out <amount> asset type not classified. Rows = each account that holds alternatives, at its alternatives part, with the yearly rate of its classified parts weighed by value (no rate when none of it is classified) and its not-classified money; for an account that is not itself an alternative (a brokerage holding a bitcoin fund or options), the row also says which part of it this is (classPortionLabel for Alternatives). The rows add up to the total (DEC-4036h, 2026-10-10).

MK-NW-O-006.name: theHolding
MK-NW-O-006.rule: Shares = shares of every purchase still held, added up (nothing when a purchase has no share count); a sale has already taken its shares from the purchases, oldest purchase date first (a purchase with no date last). Total paid = shares × cost per share over every purchase (× 100 for an option contract unless the holding states its own multiplier); nothing when a share count or a cost is not on record. With a price: value = shares × price (× 100 for an option contract unless the holding states its own multiplier); gain = value − total paid; return on cost = gain ÷ total paid (no figure when nothing was paid, or either is unknown). With NO price: value shown = total paid, and gain, return and the tax estimate are not given. Average paid per share = total paid ÷ (shares × that multiplier), so it is in the unit the price is quoted in (nothing with no shares, or a figure not on record). Closed = shares known and zero or less. Day change = last close − the close before, for ONE share (it is shown under the price of one share, not multiplied by shares held), and that ÷ the close before; none with fewer than two closes. Gain if sold today is split by purchase: long-term = purchases held MORE than one year; a purchase held exactly one year or less is short-term. Dividends = dividend records that name this ticker: the last 365 days, and all time. Realised gain = from the sale records of this ticker in this account, × this holding's contract multiplier.

MK-NW-O-007.name: theLookBack
MK-NW-O-007.rule: Passes the amount, the two price histories, the number of months and today to lookBack and returns its answer unchanged.

MK-NW-O-008.name: thePerformance
MK-NW-O-008.rule: Records of the period = those dated on or after its first day; contributions, withdrawals, dividends and interest are their totals. Contributions also count cash or shares transferred in from an account that is not one of those measured, and the first recorded value of an account that joined the record inside the period (its own records up to that day are then not counted again); withdrawals also count cash or shares transferred out. A transfer between two measured accounts is neither. THE BEGINNING IS READ from the daily record at the day BEFORE the period opens, and only when investment accounts are named and the record's first day is on or before that day; the value read is the last recorded day on or before it. If it cannot be read and the record holds days for these accounts that begin after the period opens: NO walk (no beginning, no wealth generated), and a sentence: The record begins <its first day>, so it cannot say what this account was / these accounts were worth on <the day before the period>. If it cannot be read and there is no record of these accounts at all: beginning = ending − priced gain − contributions + withdrawals (priced gain counts as 0 when the period opens today). The priced gain is each holding's gain over the period by the one rule for it (pricedGainOf: a holding's return is read as the period's own total, never a yearly rate), years = the period's days ÷ 365; a measured account with no holdings counts as its own holding, worth its balance — a certificate of deposit stating its rate gains by that rate, any other has no price history. With no period at all (day one) no rate is applied and a holding with no price history adds nothing. Owner decision DEC-3656, 2026-10-09: where a period is given that does not open today and any holding's gain cannot be known (it holds something, has no price history and no stated rate): NO walk (no beginning, no wealth generated), and the sentence: The beginning can't be worked back: <name> has no price history. Several names are joined with commas and "and" before the last, and say "have no price history". A holding is named by its ticker (the security's name where the ticker is a 9-character identifier); an account by its display name; a dollar gain handed in as unknown is named "a holding". Either way NO percent of any kind is given. The ending is given on its own as well, whether or not there is a walk. Walk: wealth generated = ending − beginning − contributions + withdrawals; change in investment value = wealth generated − dividends − interest. Records counted are those of the investment accounts named (a record on any other account is not money put into these investments). Return = a TIME-WEIGHTED return (owner decision, 2026-10-04: "All return should be True Weighted Return and not Dietz return."): the period, starting at the last recorded day on or before the day before it opens, is split at every day money moved in or out of those accounts; each piece = the value just before the next movement ÷ the value just after the last one; the pieces are multiplied and 1 is taken off. The record holds one value a day, taken after that day's money moved; money that moves on a day counts for that whole day (owner decision DEC-4439, 2026-10-11), so a day's link = that day's value ÷ (the previous recorded day's value + money added that day − money taken out that day). Money moving = deposits (in), withdrawals (out), cash transferred between accounts (out of the first, into the second), and shares moved in or out at what they were worth (the amount, or shares × price) when the record says which way they went. Ending = what the measured accounts are worth today, each counted whole (its balance, uninvested cash inside it included), read from the accounts handed in — a figure handed in beside them is not used, so no two screens can give two endings; with no accounts handed in, the ending handed in is used and closes the record. Today's value for the return is read from the same accounts. An account that first appears in the record inside the period counts as money in, at its first recorded value. A recorded day that is missing an account with holdings is not used; a typed balance stands until it is next recorded. It REFUSES — no percent, a sentence saying why, never another method — when: the beginning cannot be read; money moved on a day with no recorded value; a movement has no date; a deposit, withdrawal or transfer has no amount on record; shares were moved in or out and the record does not say which way or what they were worth; the previous recorded day's value + the money moved that day is zero or less while that day holds a value (nothing to grow from); or nothing was invested. For a period longer than one year — its first day earlier than one year back from today by the calendar (windowStartKey), so a period opening one year back to the day is a year and is never made yearly — and days ÷ 365 above 1, unless it is the whole-record Since period, the figure shown is the yearly rate (1 + return) to the power 1 ÷ years, − 1.

MK-PF-F-001.name: totalShares
MK-PF-F-001.rule: The shares of every purchase added up. Nothing (unknown) when any purchase has no share count — a missing figure is never counted as zero; a share count of 0 is a count.

MK-PF-F-002.name: costBasis
MK-PF-F-002.rule: Shares × cost per share, added up over every purchase, × the contract multiplier (100 for an option unless the holding states its own, otherwise 1). A purchase with no shares adds nothing. Nothing (unknown) when a purchase has no share count, or has shares and no cost per share on record; a cost per share of 0 is a figure.

MK-PF-F-003.name: avgCost
MK-PF-F-003.rule: Cost (costBasis) ÷ (shares held × the contract multiplier). Nothing when no shares are held (there is no average price), or when the shares or the cost are unknown. The cost carries an option's multiplier, so it is taken back out: the answer is per share, the unit a price is quoted in.

MK-PF-F-004.name: marketValue
MK-PF-F-004.rule: Shares × price × the contract multiplier, unrounded. 0 when no shares are held. Nothing (unknown) when there is no price, or the share count is unknown — shares with no price are worth something unknown, not 0.

MK-PF-F-005.name: unrealizedGain
MK-PF-F-005.rule: Market value − cost. Nothing (unknown) when there is no price, or the market value or the cost is unknown.

MK-PF-F-006.name: capGains
MK-PF-F-006.rule: With no price: all three are nothing (unknown). Purchases with no shares held are passed over. For each other purchase: gain = shares × (price − cost per share) × the contract multiplier (100 for an option unless the holding states its own, otherwise 1). It is long-term when today is after the first anniversary of the purchase date — held MORE than one year — and short-term otherwise (a purchase on the leap day has its anniversary on the last day of February the next year, so a sale on the first of March is long-term); a purchase with no valid date counts as short-term. A purchase with no cost on record (none, or a cost per share of 0 or less) or no share count makes ITS part (long-term or short-term, by its date) nothing (unknown), and the total with it. Returns the long-term total, the short-term total and their sum.

MK-PF-F-007.name: totalROI
MK-PF-F-007.rule: Unrealised gain ÷ cost. Nothing when there is no price, the cost is unknown or zero or less, or the gain is unknown.

MK-PF-F-008.name: startDateFor
MK-PF-F-008.rule: 1M, 3M and 6M: today moved back that many months; 1Y and 2Y: back 12 or 24 months — the same day of that month, or its last day when that month is shorter (one month before 31 March is 28 February; a year before 29 February is 28 February). This year: 1 January of today's year. Any other label: today.

MK-PF-F-009.name: latestClose
MK-PF-F-009.rule: The close of the last price on record; nothing when there are no prices.

MK-PF-F-010.name: periodReturn
MK-PF-F-010.rule: End = the latest close. The beginning day = the day BEFORE the period's start date (both boundary days are inside the period). Start = the last close on or before the beginning day — or, when every price on record is later than that day, the FIRST close on record. Return = end ÷ start − 1. For 2Y it is given as a yearly rate. When the prices reach back to the beginning day: (end ÷ start) to the power one half, − 1. When they do not: the yearly rate over the span the prices do cover — (end ÷ start) to the power 1 ÷ years, − 1, where years = the days from the first price to the last ÷ 365.25 — and only when that span is more than one year; a span of a year or less keeps its own total. Nothing when there are no prices or the start close is zero or less. The same move is also given as the period's own total, never a yearly rate, for anything that adds holdings up.

MK-PF-F-011.name: periodReturnSince
MK-PF-F-011.rule: The same as periodReturn but measured from a given date: latest close ÷ the last close on or before that date (or the first close on record when all are later), − 1. Never turned into a yearly rate.

MK-PF-F-012.name: earliestPurchaseDate
MK-PF-F-012.rule: The earliest purchase date among the holding's purchases that carry a valid date; nothing when none does.

MK-PF-F-013.name: benchmarkTicker
MK-PF-F-013.rule: The market yardstick for a holding, handed its kind (or the holding itself). The class decides first where the person set it, or where no kind names a yardstick: a bond → AGG; stocks and funds → SPY. Otherwise by kind: stocks and funds → SPY; fixed income and annuities → AGG; private equity → PSP; hedge funds → QAI; commodities → GLD; crypto → BTC; 529, 401(k), traditional and Roth IRA and HSA → AOR; other → SPY. A kind or class that names no yardstick → SPY. NOTHING when nothing says what the holding is (no kind, no class) — no yardstick, and its comparison refuses.

MK-PF-F-014.name: buildPerformance
MK-PF-F-014.rule: For each holding: price = latest close; market value, cost, unrealised gain and return on cost from the functions above (each nothing where unknown). Bought = its earliest purchase date, or the date supplied when it has none. If it was bought ON OR AFTER the period's start day it is capped: its period return is time-weighted from its purchases — the purchases grouped by day (an undated one on the first day); the first piece starts at what was paid; at each later purchase day the piece ends at the shares then held × the close on or before that day, and the next starts there plus what that purchase paid; the last ends at shares held × today's price; the pieces multiplied, − 1 (one purchase day gives the return on cost; nothing when a share count or cost is missing or a purchase day has no close) — and the yardstick is measured since the first purchase date. Otherwise its period return is the price return over the period (periodReturn, a yearly rate over 2Y), and the yardstick is measured over the same period. Each row also carries the period's own total for the holding and for the yardstick (never a yearly rate). No yardstick (nothing says what the holding is): no yardstick return. Beat-by = the holding's return − the yardstick's; nothing when either is missing.

MK-PF-F-015.name: topHoldingConcentration
MK-PF-F-015.rule: Nothing when any holding's value is unknown, when total value is zero or less, or when there are fewer than two holdings. Otherwise the holding with the largest value, its value (unrounded), and its share of the total — reported only when the UNROUNDED share is 25% or more; the share is returned as a whole percent, the figure as shown.

MK-PF-F-016.name: attribution
MK-PF-F-016.rule: For each holding with a return over the period above −100% and a value above zero: its value at the start = its value now ÷ (1 + its return over the whole period, never a yearly rate); weight = that ÷ the starts added up; contribution = weight × its return. Sorted, largest contribution first. Empty when the starts add up to zero or less.

MK-PF-F-017.name: allocation
MK-PF-F-017.rule: Empty when any holding's value is unknown. Value by kind of holding (a holding with no kind counts as other), plus cash when above zero. Share = value ÷ total × 100, unrounded. Sorted, largest first. Empty when the total is zero or less.

MK-PF-F-018.name: portfolioTrend
MK-PF-F-018.rule: Empty with no holdings, or when any holding's share count is unknown. Thirteen evenly spaced dates from the period's start to today. Value at each date = TODAY'S share count × the close on or before that date, added over the holdings (a holding with no price counts as zero). Yardstick line = the starting value × (yardstick close ÷ its close at the start); it equals the value line where the yardstick has no price.

MK-PF-F-019.name: portfolioPeriodReturn
MK-PF-F-019.rule: Over the holdings that have a return over the period above −100% and a value above zero: each one's value at the start = its value now ÷ (1 + its return over the whole period, never a yearly rate); the answer = the values now added up ÷ the values at the start added up − 1. Nothing when there are none.

MK-PF-F-020.name: portfolioBenchReturn
MK-PF-F-020.rule: Over the holdings that have their own return over the period above −100%, a value above zero, and a yardstick return: each one's value at the start = its value now ÷ (1 + its own return over the whole period); the yardstick returns (over the whole period, never a yearly rate) averaged, weighted by those start values. A holding with no return of its own is left out. Nothing when there are none.

MK-PF-F-021.name: periodDollarDelta
MK-PF-F-021.rule: The dollars a return stands for: today's total × return ÷ (1 + return), unrounded. Nothing when the return is missing or either input is not a number, or the return is −100% or worse.

MK-PF-F-022.name: factorOverMonths
MK-PF-F-022.rule: Nothing with fewer than two prices. Cut-off = today moved back the given number of months — the same day of that month, or its last day when that month is shorter. Nothing when the first price on record is later than the cut-off — the record does not reach back that far. Start = the last price on or before the cut-off. Factor = latest close ÷ start close; nothing when the start close is zero or less.

MK-PF-F-023.name: lookBack
MK-PF-F-023.rule: Nothing unless the amount is above zero and both funds have a factor (factorOverMonths). Stayed: end value = amount × the factor of the fund it was in; change = end value − amount; percent = (factor − 1) × 100, at full precision. Moved: the same with the other fund's factor. Difference = moved end value − stayed end value.

MK-PF-F-028.name: realizedFromLedger
MK-PF-F-028.rule: Uses buy, opening-position and sale records that name a ticker, with shares above zero and a price, for the ticker and account asked for, in date order. A sale is matched to the earliest purchases first, within one account and one ticker. Gain on a sale = (matched shares × sale price − what those shares cost) × the contract multiplier of the holding asked about (100 for an option unless it states its own; 1 when no holding is named). All-time = every sale; this year = sales dated in today's calendar year. A sale of more shares than the purchases on record counts only the matched part and is tallied as a sale without a cost on record.

MK-PF-F-029.name: closeAsOf
MK-PF-F-029.rule: The close of the last price dated on or before the target date. When every price on record is later than the target, the FIRST close on record. Nothing with no prices.

MK-PF-F-031.name: contractMultiplier
MK-PF-F-031.rule: The holding's own multiplier when it states one above zero; otherwise 100 for an option and 1 for everything else.

MK-PF-F-032.name: quantityUnit
MK-PF-F-032.rule: The person's own unit where they entered one; otherwise coins for crypto, contracts for options, ounces for commodities, and shares for everything else.

MK-PF-F-033.name: quantityWithUnit
MK-PF-F-033.rule: The quantity followed by its unit (quantityUnit); the unit loses its final s when the quantity is exactly 1. Nothing (refused) when the quantity is not on record, not a number, or below zero — the app has no words for a short (written) position.

MK-PF-F-034.name: closeOnOrBefore
MK-PF-F-034.rule: The close of the last price dated on or before the given day. Nothing when there is none, when there are no prices, or when the day is not written as year-month-day.

MK-CF-O-019.name: theIncomeManager
MK-CF-O-019.rule: Takes the ten sources in the picker's order — a job, self-employment, rent, interest and dividends, retirement income, benefits, support, scholarships, student loans, something else — gives each one figure, and splits them into entered (a figure above zero) and not entered. A job: the household's monthly take-home (basePay) over the earners who have a wage, named after those earners, and marked as calculated when any part of it is. Self-employment: the amount as entered, per month or per year. Rent: rent after running costs for the year (rentalNetAnnual) ÷ 12, per month, with how many properties (1 property; the plural from plural, the one list of words — his ruling of 2026-10-10). Interest and dividends: the yearly amount, marked reinvested or paid to the bank. Retirement income: the monthly total (retirementIncomeMonthly). Benefits: the monthly benefit, saying how many months when fewer than 12. Support: the monthly amount. Scholarships: monthly ones × 12 plus yearly ones, per year. Student loans: each loan × the number of months it arrives in (1 when it names none), per year. Something else: the amount as entered — per month, per year or one-time. Bonus and stock, only when there is a job: the yearly bonus + the stock that vests in a year (rsuAnnual), and the month the bonus is paid (December when none is set).

MK-NW-F-105.name: whyNoReturn
MK-NW-F-105.rule: The sentence shown where a time-weighted return cannot be measured; empty when it was measured. Money moved on a day with no recorded value: names the day and says a return cannot be measured across it. A movement with no date: says so. A deposit or withdrawal with no amount on record: names the day and says a return cannot be measured across it. Shares moved in or out: names the day and says the records do not say what they were worth. Nothing to grow from on a day (the previous evening's value + money added − money taken out is zero or less while that day holds a value): names the day and says which — a value recorded with nothing there the evening before and no money added, or more money taken out than was there the evening before plus the money added that day. Since DEC-4439 (2026-10-11) a value below the money added is a loss, measured, and has no sentence. Nothing invested over the period: says there is no return to state. Today's value not on record: says so. A beginning that cannot be read has no sentence here — the period is shown as not covered instead.

MK-NW-F-104.name: closedWith
MK-NW-F-104.rule: The daily record with today added: one row per account that the latest earlier recorded day holds (of the accounts named), carrying between them the ending value handed in. The record is returned unchanged when there is no earlier day or it holds none of those accounts. It adds no arithmetic: it lets a return be measured to today when the caller gave an ending value and no accounts.

MK-NW-F-106.name: mortgagesByProperty
MK-NW-F-106.rule: Properties = the accounts whose class is real estate. Mortgages = the debts whose type is mortgage. Owner rule, 2026-10-04: "It is feasible to have property without mortgage but no mortgage without property. So check should be 3 properties in NW - 3 or less mortgage." A mortgage is on the property it names, when that property exists and has no mortgage placed on it yet. A mortgage that names no property is placed only where there is one answer: first, on the one property without a mortgage whose name its own name begins with; then, when exactly one property is still without a mortgage and exactly one mortgage is still without a property, on that property. Every other mortgage is listed as on no property — including a second mortgage that names a property already taken. It gives: the count of properties and of mortgages; for each property its mortgage (or none) and that mortgage's required monthly payment; the mortgages on no property; whether there are none of those; and the sentence to show when there are.

MK-NW-F-107.name: propertyUses
MK-NW-F-107.rule: For each property: what it is used for, as propertyUseMap reads it, handed the rent entries from the Income screen (none handed in when the person has none on record). Owner rule, 2026-10-04: "unless rental income is added on the income screen, assume property is second or vacation home." RENTAL = a rent entry names it — or, only when no rent entries are handed in at all, it is stored as a rental. HOME = the one marked as the home lived in; with none marked and no use stated on any, the one entered first. SECOND = every other property, except that a rent entry naming no property makes the one remaining property a rental when there is exactly one.

MK-CF-O-020.name: theBudgetCounted
MK-CF-O-020.rule: Owner rule, 2026-10-04: "Once user enters mortgage or any debt - the app deduct it directly to calculate surplus, emergency fund, and any other place instead of leaving it for user to add it to planned expenses." The home = the property read as HOME (propertyUses, handed the profile's rent entries — none recorded is read as none, not as unknown). Its mortgage = the mortgage matched to that property (mortgagesByProperty). When the home has a mortgage in Debts AND the budget's Rent / Mortgage line holds an amount: that line is counted as nothing, the one typed monthly total (when there is one) is lowered by the same amount, never below zero, and the sentence says the line is not counted and names the mortgage. Otherwise — a renter, a home with no mortgage, a mortgage on another property, or no amount on the line — the budget is counted exactly as typed. It also names the home's mortgage when there is one. What the person typed is never changed; this is the budget as it is counted.

MK-NW-F-108.name: taxWordsOf
MK-NW-F-108.rule: The words for how an account is taxed, shown on its page. A 529 always reads tax-free for education; an HSA always reads pre-tax — tax-free for medical costs, whatever treatment is stated. Otherwise by its treatment (taxTreatmentOf): tax type not stated reads tax type not stated (DEC-4036f, 2026-10-10); tax-deferred reads pre-tax — taxed when it comes out; tax-free reads tax-free (Roth) for an account in the Roth bucket and tax-free for any other; taxable reads taxable.

MK-NW-F-109.name: holdingClassOf
MK-NW-F-109.rule: The class of one holding inside an account. What was stored: the broker's or importer's tag (bond → Bonds & CDs, other → Alternatives, cash → cash, any other tag → Stocks / Funds), else the class of the kind picked when it was added (not real estate or personal property), else nothing. (1) If the person said what it is, their answer — the stored class, or Unclassified when nothing is stored. (2) If it is marked as asked, Unclassified (owner rule, 2026-09-30: "Refuse the line and ask"). (3) The class its ticker and name are evidence for, unless that is cash: a money-market fund is Stocks / Funds, a CD or a T-bill is Bonds & CDs, whatever tag the broker sent (owner rule, 2026-08-04: cash means cash only). (4) Otherwise what was stored; with nothing stored, cash when the name says cash, else Unclassified — never a guessed Stocks / Funds.

MK-NW-F-110.name: primaryHomeIdOf
MK-NW-F-110.rule: The property propertyUseMap reads as the home lived in, handed the rent entries when the caller has them. Nothing (null) when the household has no home — which is not the same as not being asked.

MK-NW-F-111.name: assetsStateFrom
MK-NW-F-111.rule: buildAssetsState of the saved accounts. Nothing when there is no saved record, or the saved record holds no accounts.

MK-NW-F-112.name: yearlyInterest
MK-NW-F-112.rule: A year's interest from one bond or CD. Nothing when no rate was entered. Face value × rate when a face value was entered; otherwise today's value × rate.

MK-NW-F-113.name: altPartsOf
MK-NW-F-113.rule: The alternatives inside one account, each with the kind its yearly rate is read from. An account that is itself an alternative: its alternatives part of the class split (or its whole balance when it has no split), at its own kind. Any other account: each option at its synced value, kind options; each holding classed as an alternative with a price, shares × price, kind crypto when its name says bitcoin, ethereum or crypto, commodities when it says gold, silver, platinum, palladium or commodity, otherwise other; and whatever of the account's alternatives part is left (more than half a cent either way) is a part with no kind, marked asset type not classified — never other, and given no rate (DEC-4036h, 2026-10-10). Nothing when the account holds no alternatives.

MK-NW-F-114.name: rentAmount
MK-NW-F-114.rule: A rent figure as a number. Owner rule, 2026-10-10: a rent figure is a number. It is read only when it is a plain number: digits with at most one decimal point, allowing a leading dollar sign, thousands commas and spaces. A figure with letters or any other text in it (a word such as "about", a "k" for thousands, "n/a", a minus sign) is not read and counts as not entered, never as the digits inside it. Not entered, blank or missing gives 0.

MK-NW-F-115.name: liveRent
MK-NW-F-115.rule: The rent entries that name their property (a property identifier that is not blank) and whose rent coming in or costs going out is above zero. An entry that names no property is not rent and is left out, whatever its figures (owner rule DEC-4059d, 2026-10-10).

MK-NW-F-116.name: rentedIdsOf
MK-NW-F-116.rule: The identifiers of the properties the live rent entries name.

MK-NW-F-117.name: propertyUseMap
MK-NW-F-117.rule: For each real-estate account: rental when a live rent entry names it, or — only when no rent entries were handed in at all (unknown, not none) — when it is stored as a rental. Of the rest: the one marked as the home lived in is home; with none marked and no other use stated (a stored 'rental' word does not count here), the one entered first (last in the list) that is not stored as a rental is home — a property stored as a rental is never made the home this way. Every other property is a second home. A rent entry that names no property makes no property a rental (owner rule DEC-4059d, 2026-10-10 — it used to make the one other property a rental when exactly one remained).

MK-NW-F-118.name: itemizeMissingCount
MK-NW-F-118.rule: How many listed holdings have no value (none entered, or not a number). A remainder worked out while any are missing is not final.

MK-NW-F-119.name: estimatedAccrued
MK-NW-F-119.rule: The interest earned since the last yearly coupon, estimated from the coupon schedule: face × rate × the days since the last maturity anniversary ÷ the days in that coupon year, with the days. Nothing for a CD bought from the bank (a CD bought through a broker is estimated like a bond, DEC-3837, 2026-10-10), a bond with no face or no rate above zero, no maturity date or a day that does not exist, a matured bond, or on a coupon day (nothing has accrued).

MK-NW-F-124.name: maturityParts
MK-NW-F-124.rule: A maturity date read as a real calendar day: its year, month and day, when the date is written year-month-day and that day exists on the calendar. Nothing when there is no date, it is written another way, or the day does not exist (a day past the end of its month, or a month past December).

MK-NW-F-125.name: isPastMaturity
MK-NW-F-125.rule: Yes when the bond's maturity date is a real calendar day earlier than today's date on the device; no when it is today or later. No date, or a day that does not exist, is unknown, so the answer is no — never matured.

MK-NW-F-126.name: yearlyInterestNow
MK-NW-F-126.rule: A year's interest from one bond or CD as it pays today: $0 once it is past its maturity date; otherwise its yearly interest (face × rate, or the value × rate when no face was entered), and nothing when no rate was entered.

MK-NW-F-120.name: classEvidenceOf
MK-NW-F-120.rule: What an account's own facts say its class is, before its kind is looked at. A maturity date that reads as a real date (the same reading as MK-NW-F-009 maturityClass: a text that is not a real date counts as no date, DEC-4059b/c, 2026-10-10) makes it Bonds & CDs. Otherwise a property — a home, real estate, a vehicle, or anything in the property group — gives nothing, because its name is a place, not evidence. Otherwise what its name is evidence for, or nothing.

figures_checked_by_hand.009: not a figure: the identifier MK-NW-F-009 of maturityClass, which this function asks

MK-NW-F-121.name: holdingTagClass
MK-NW-F-121.rule: The class a holding's stored tag means: bond is Bonds & CDs, other is Alternatives, cash is Cash, any other tag is Stocks / Funds, and no tag is nothing.

MK-NW-F-122.name: holdingTagFor
MK-NW-F-122.rule: The tag a holding is stored under for a class, the reverse of the reading above: Bonds & CDs is bond, Alternatives is other, Cash is cash, Stocks / Funds is stock_etf; any other class has no tag.

MK-NW-F-123.name: holdingNameEvidence
MK-NW-F-123.rule: What a holding's ticker and description, read together, are evidence for — a class, or nothing when the words name none.

MK-NW-F-127.name: gainOfRow
MK-NW-F-127.rule: What one holding gained over the window, or nothing when that cannot be known. Bought inside the window: its own gain (value less cost). With a return for the period: the return over the WHOLE window (the window total the row carries; else, when the window is longer than one year, the yearly rate compounded over the window's years — (1 + rate) to the power years − 1; else the return as given); then value now × (1 − 1 ÷ (1 + that)), and $0 when it holds nothing. A CD with a stated rate above zero: value now × (1 − 1 ÷ (1 + the rate) to the power of the window's years), and $0 when it holds nothing. Otherwise: $0 when it holds nothing (heldValueOf is 0), and nothing (unknown) when it holds something or its worth is unknown — a holding with no price history and no rate.

MK-NW-F-128.name: heldValueOf
MK-NW-F-128.rule: What a holding is worth when no price history prices it: its market value when that is above zero; else its shares (totalShares) × the broker's last price × the contract multiplier (100 for an option unless it states its own) when there is a last price — nothing when the shares are unknown; else the value it was last built at; else $0 when it holds no shares; else NOTHING (unknown) — shares with no price.

MK-NW-F-129.name: gainRowName
MK-NW-F-129.rule: What the sentence calls a holding: the name it was given; else its ticker — unless the ticker is a security code (nine letters and digits in either case, with a digit in it) and the holding has a name, when the name is used; else its name; else "a holding".

MK-NW-F-130.name: cannotWorkBackSentence
MK-NW-F-130.rule: The sentence when the beginning cannot be worked back: "The beginning can't be worked back: <names> has no price history." Each name is listed once, however many times it is handed in. With several names, they are joined by commas with "and" before the last, and the verb is "have". With no name, "a holding".

MK-NW-F-131.name: pricedLikeBond
MK-NW-F-131.rule: Yes for every bond that is not a CD. For a CD: yes only when it was bought through a broker; a CD bought from the bank, or one whose answer was never given, is no (DEC-3837, 2026-10-10). This is the one test every bond figure reads to decide whether a CD is priced like a bond.

figures_checked_by_hand.3837: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-3837 (2026-10-10) that this rule follows

MK-ST-F-080.name: isDay
MK-ST-F-080.rule: True only when the value is text written exactly as four digits, a dash, two digits, a dash and two digits (year-month-day) AND that day exists in the calendar (2026-02-29 and 2026-02-31 are false; 2024-02-29 is true). Anything else is false: a number, nothing at all, or a date with a time written after it.

MK-ST-F-081.name: timeWeightedReturn
MK-ST-F-081.rule: Works from the daily record, which holds one value per account per day, taken after that day's money moved; the previous usable day stands for the evening before. Days after the last day asked for, and days not written as year-month-day (isDay), are ignored. Each measured account has its own line of values, from its first recorded day to its last. The total on a day = the values that day of the measured accounts whose line covers that day. An account that has ever held a priced security must have a value on that very day, or the day is not used at all; any other account (a typed or cash balance) keeps its last earlier value until its next one. THE BEGINNING = the latest recorded day on or before the start day whose total can be formed with at least one account in it; with none it refuses (the start is not recorded). The last day asked for must be in the record and its total formed, or it refuses (the end is not recorded). It refuses when a deposit or withdrawal on a measured account that is not cash has no year-month-day date, when shares were moved on any day after the beginning up to the last day (naming the first such day), and when a deposit, withdrawal or transfer with no amount on record is dated after the beginning up to the last day (naming the first such day). THE PIECES: from the beginning, take each later usable day in order. Money in on that day, account by account: an account there now but not on the previous usable day joined the record: it brings in the money added to it that day when there is any (it was worth nothing the evening before, so that money is its base — DEC-4439), otherwise its whole value; one there before but not now takes out its last value (it left); a cash account brings in its change in value less the interest credited to it after the previous usable day up to this day (cash earns only interest); any other account brings in its deposits (plus) and withdrawals (minus) dated after the previous usable day up to this day, and if one of those is dated before this day it refuses, naming that day (money moved on a day with no recorded value). THE DAY'S LINK (owner decision DEC-4439, 2026-10-11: money that moves on a day counts for that whole day): the base = the previous usable day's total + money in. When the base is more than half a cent, the growth so far is multiplied by this day's total (never below zero) ÷ the base, and the measured period starts at the previous day if it has not started yet — or at this day when the previous total was half a cent or less (the first money's day). When the base is half a cent or less: if it is below minus half a cent, or this day's total is more than half a cent either way, it refuses, naming the day (nothing to grow from), and says when more was taken out than the previous total plus the money added; otherwise nothing is measured for that piece. When no piece was measured it refuses (nothing invested). THE RETURN = the pieces multiplied together − 1, as a share at full precision (not a percent, and never turned into a yearly rate here), with the day the measured period started. It never falls back to another method.

MK-ST-F-082.name: movementsOf
MK-ST-F-082.rule: Sorts a household's records, for the accounts being measured, into money moving in or out, interest, and days shares were moved. Each record's date is its first ten characters. A deposit or withdrawal on a measured account with NO amount (missing or not a number) is not money in or out at all: its day goes on the list of days with an amount missing, and the return refuses there; the same for a transfer with no amount that crosses the edge of the measured accounts (one side measured, the other not). That list is handed back only when it has a day on it. Any other missing or unreadable amount counts as zero. A deposit on a measured account is money in (plus its amount); a withdrawal on one is money out (minus its amount) — the sign comes from the kind of record, so a withdrawal written as a negative amount becomes money in. A transfer is money out of its first account when that account is measured, and money into its second account when that one is measured, so a transfer between two measured accounts appears as both. Shares moved (a transfer in kind): nothing when both accounts named are measured, or neither is, or when only one account is named and it is not measured. Otherwise it is money into or out of the measured account at what the shares were worth — the record's amount when above zero, else shares × price: in when they arrive in the measured account (or, with one account named, when the record says in), out when they leave (or the record says out). When the direction is neither in nor out, or the worth is not above zero, the day goes on the list of days shares were moved instead. Interest on a measured account that was not reinvested is interest (plus its amount). Every other kind of record is ignored. Each movement keeps its own day; the time-weighted return counts it for that whole day (DEC-4439, 2026-10-11).

MK-PF-F-035.name: unknownFigure
MK-PF-F-035.rule: A purchase's figure (its shares or its cost per share) counts as never entered when it is missing, or is not a number, or is not a finite number (for example infinity). Then the answer is yes. A real figure, zero included, gives no.

MK-PF-F-036.name: monthsBefore
MK-PF-F-036.rule: Go back the given number of months from today's date, crossing into earlier years when needed, and keep the same day of the month and the same time of day. When that day does not exist in the earlier month (the 31st in a month of 30 days, or the 29th of February in a year without one), use that month's last day instead — never roll over into the next month.

MK-PF-F-037.name: dayBefore
MK-PF-F-037.rule: The calendar day before the given day, at the same time of day. The first of a month gives the last day of the month before; the first of January gives the last day of December of the year before.

MK-PF-F-038.name: periodTotalReturn
MK-PF-F-038.rule: The price move over the period as the period's own total, never turned into a yearly rate: the same total that periodReturn starts from (latest close ÷ the close at the beginning − 1, read by periodReturnParts). Nothing when there are no prices, no latest close, no close at the beginning, or that close is zero or less.

MK-PF-F-039.name: periodReturnParts
MK-PF-F-039.rule: Nothing when there are no prices. End = the latest close. The beginning day = the day BEFORE the period's start date (both boundary days are inside the period). Start = the last close on or before the beginning day. Nothing when end or start is missing, or start is zero or less. Total = end ÷ start − 1. Years: 1 for every period except 2Y (1 means it is never turned into a yearly rate). For 2Y: when the first price on record is on or before the beginning day, years = 2; when it is later, years = the time from the first price to the last price, in days ÷ 365.25. The answer is the total and the years.

MK-PF-F-040.name: returnSincePurchases
MK-PF-F-040.rule: A holding bought inside the period, time-weighted from its purchases. Nothing when there is no price today. Every purchase must have a share count and a cost per share that are real numbers, or the answer is nothing. Purchases of zero or fewer shares are skipped. Each purchase is placed on its own date (the date's year-month-day part), or on the period's first purchase day handed in when its date is missing or unreadable; purchases on the same day are added together: shares added, and paid = shares × cost per share added. Nothing when no purchase is left. Walk the days from earliest to latest, starting with shares held 0, money in the piece 0, growth 1. On the first day: money in the piece = what was paid that day. On each later day: take the last close on or before that day (nothing if there is none, or if the money in the piece is zero or less); growth = growth × (shares held × that close) ÷ money in the piece; then money in the piece = shares held × that close + what was paid that day. After each day, shares held grows by that day's shares. At the end: nothing when the money in the piece is zero or less; otherwise the return = growth × (shares held × today's price) ÷ money in the piece − 1. With a single purchase day this is today's value ÷ what was paid − 1.

MK-PF-F-041.name: isoDay
MK-PF-F-041.rule: A date written as the person's own local calendar day: the year, a dash, the month number (January is 1) written with two digits, a dash, the day of the month written with two digits — a single digit gets a 0 in front.

MK-PF-F-042.name: windowTotal
MK-PF-F-042.rule: A holding's return over the whole window, never a yearly rate. When the row carries its window total (even an empty one), that total is the answer as written. Otherwise: nothing when there is no return. When the window is longer than one year (years above 1): (1 + the yearly rate) to the power years, − 1. Otherwise the return itself. Years not handed in counts as 0, so the return is used as it stands.

MK-PF-F-043.name: windowTotalOfRow
MK-PF-F-043.rule: One holding's return over the whole window: windowTotal read with the row's period return and the row's period total, and no years. So the row's period total when it carries one (even an empty one); otherwise its period return as it stands; nothing when it has neither.

MK-PF-F-044.name: startValues
MK-PF-F-044.rule: For each holding row, read its return over the window. Keep the row only when that return is known, is above −1 (a loss of less than everything), and the holding's value today is above zero; every other row is left out. For each row kept: its value when the window began = today's value ÷ (1 + the return). The answer is the list of rows kept, each with its return and that starting value. No rows gives an empty list.
